knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an iterative method produce \(x_c,x_+\in\mathbb R^n\) for differentiable \(f\). Let \(s_i>0\), \(F>0\), and tolerances \(\tau_g,\tau_x>0\) be supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision stopping organization for smooth unconstrained minimization using scaled local information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[G(x_+):=\max_i\frac{|\nabla_i f(x_+)|\max\{|(x_+)_i|,s_i\}}{\max\{|f(x_+)|,F\}},\qquad S(x_c,x_+):=\max_i\frac{|(x_+)_i-(x_c)_i|}{\max\{|(x_+)_i|,s_i\}}.\] A practical test system reports gradient stationarity when \(G(x_+)\le\tau_g\), and reports step stagnation or convergence when \(S(x_c,x_+)\le\tau_x\). The two outcomes are distinct: the first is an approximate optimality test, whereas the second only states that successive scaled iterates are close. A second-order diagnostic may subsequently test whether the Hessian is positive definite or has negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The system combines a scale-aware relative-gradient test with a scale-aware relative-step test. A small scaled gradient is the primary stationarity condition. A small step is a separate termination signal because it may represent either convergence or algorithmic stalling. Curvature information is needed if one must distinguish a local minimum from a maximum or saddle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system returns the pair \((G(x_+)\le\tau_g,\ S(x_c,x_+)\le\tau_x)\), preserving the distinction between approximate stationarity and lack of iterate movement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(D_+=\operatorname{diag}(\max\{|(x_+)_i|,s_i\})\), \(S(x_c,x_+)=\|D_+^{-1}(x_+-x_c)\|_\infty\).
special_cases_latex: If exact derivatives are unavailable, \(\nabla f(x_+)\) may be replaced by a computed gradient, with a tolerance reflecting its error.
A Hessian positive-definiteness check can be attached after the gradient test to screen approximate maxima and saddles.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small step without a small scaled gradient must not be interpreted as first-order stationarity.
The use of \(s_i\) prevents coordinates whose natural magnitudes are near zero from producing singular relative changes.
boundary_notes: These stopping tests do not certify global optimality.
A positive-definite approximate Hessian test depends on derivative and eigenvalue accuracy and is not part of the two primary Boolean tests.

children.title: Gradient-Based Stopping Measures
children.top_down_role: First-order termination mechanisms and their scaled variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Based Stopping Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unscaled and diagonally scaled first-order termination measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a differentiable objective, the unscaled first-order stopping measure is \(m_g(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\). Given an invertible diagonal scaling matrix \(D\), define the scaled measure
\[m_{g,D}(x)=\|D^{-1}\nabla f(x)\|_2.\]
An algorithm declares first-order termination at tolerance \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\) when \(m_g(x)\le\varepsilon_g\), or under the declared scaling convention when \(m_{g,D}(x)\le\varepsilon_g\). The scaling matrix and norm must remain fixed when reported tolerances are compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order termination occurs when either the gradient norm or a declared scaled gradient norm is below its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an explicitly declared invertible diagonal scaling matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is accepted when the selected measure does not exceed \(\varepsilon_g\).

notation.meaning: Declared diagonal variable or gradient scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Aware Stopping Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined approximate first- and second-order stationarity measure.

For \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\) and positive tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H\), define
\[m_2(x)=\max\left\{ rac{\|
abla f(x)\|_2}{\varepsilon_g}, rac{\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 f(x))\}}{\varepsilon_H}ight\}.\]
Curvature-aware termination is accepted exactly when \(m_2(x)\le1\). Equivalently, \(\|
abla f(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 f(x))\ge-\varepsilon_H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination requires both a small gradient and absence of Hessian curvature more negative than the declared curvature tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_2(x)\le1\) if and only if \(x\) satisfies the declared approximate second-order conditions.

children.title: Finite-Precision Stopping Floors
children.top_down_role: Numerical limits on meaningful stationarity tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Stopping Floors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-error floor for meaningful derivative-based tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose computed quantities \(\widehat g\) and \(\widehat\lambda\) satisfy
\[\|\widehat g-\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\delta_g,\qquad |\widehat\lambda-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))|\le\delta_H.\]
Then
\[\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\|\widehat g\|_2+\delta_g,\qquad\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\ge\widehat\lambda-\delta_H.\]
Consequently, computed residuals alone cannot certify gradient or curvature tolerances materially below \(\delta_g\) or \(\delta_H\). A sound stopping test must incorporate these error bounds or use tolerances no smaller than the corresponding numerical floors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative errors impose stopping floors: reported gradient and curvature tolerances below their error bounds are not certifiable from computed quantities alone.
assumptions_latex: The computed gradient has normwise error at most \(\delta_g\).
The computed smallest Hessian eigenvalue has absolute error at most \(\delta_H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reliable stopping bounds must include \(\delta_g\) and \(\delta_H\); smaller tolerances are unsupported by the computed data alone.

notation.meaning: Certified gradient and eigenvalue error bounds.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let objective evaluations have relative noise level \(\eta\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\), and suppose the gradient used in a stopping test is computed by finite differences.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational finite-precision floor for finite-difference gradient stopping in smooth unconstrained minimization; it is not a universal lower bound for analytic derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the finite-difference gradient stopping floor by \[\tau_{g,\mathrm{floor}}:=\sqrt{\eta}.\] A requested scaled-gradient tolerance \(\tau_g\) is numerically meaningful for this derivative regime only when \(\tau_g\ge\tau_{g,\mathrm{floor}}\); if \(\tau_g<\sqrt\eta\), the stopping test may be unattainable because the computed gradient cannot reliably resolve that scale. When \(d\) reliable decimal digits are supplied, the noise model may be set to \(\eta=\max\{\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}},10^{-d}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For gradients formed by finite differences from noisy objective values, the practical scaled-gradient tolerance has a noise-dependent floor of approximately the square root of the relative objective noise. Asking for a smaller tolerance may prevent termination even when the true gradient is smaller, because the computed derivative cannot resolve it reliably.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta\) is a bound or working estimate for relative noise in objective evaluations.
The stopping gradient is approximated by finite differences.
The scaled-gradient test uses a positive tolerance \(\tau_g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_g\ge\sqrt\eta\) is the operational attainability condition for the finite-difference scaled-gradient test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(d\) reliable decimal digits are assumed, \(\tau_{g,\mathrm{floor}}=\sqrt{\max\{\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}},10^{-d}\}}\).
special_cases_latex: For full-precision objective values modeled by \(\eta=\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\), the finite-difference floor is \(\sqrt{\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Tightening \(\tau_g\) below the floor does not create a more reliable certificate.
Derivative accuracy, rather than the exact mathematical stationarity condition, controls the meaningful numerical tolerance.
boundary_notes: The source describes \(\sqrt\eta\) as likely to be the smallest satisfiable finite-difference tolerance, not as an absolute impossibility theorem.
Analytic, automatic-differentiation, complex-step, stochastic, or higher-order derivative estimators can have different floors.

notation.meaning: Estimated relative noise in objective values.
Unit roundoff or machine precision parameter.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\) near \(x_*\), and set \(g_*=\nabla f(x_*)\), \(H_*=\nabla^2f(x_*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local classification of smooth unconstrained critical points using local order and Hessian spectral information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A critical point is a point \(x_*\) with \(g_*=0\). It is a local minimum if \(f(x_*)\le f(x)\) near \(x_*\), a strict local minimum if the inequality is strict for every nearby \(x\ne x_*\), and a local maximum by reversing the inequality. It is a saddle when every neighborhood contains points \(y,z\) satisfying \(f(y)<f(x_*)<f(z)\). Spectrally, write \(\operatorname{In}(H_*)=(n_+,n_-,n_0)\). Positive-definite and negative-definite Hessians identify nondegenerate strict minima and maxima; \(n_+>0\) and \(n_->0\) identify an indefinite saddle; and \(n_0>0\) marks degeneracy, for which Hessian signs alone may not determine the local type.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy first identifies critical points by a zero gradient, then classifies their nearby objective ordering as minimum, maximum, or saddle. The Hessian inertia refines the classification: all positive eigenvalues indicate a nondegenerate minimum, all negative eigenvalues a nondegenerate maximum, mixed signs a saddle, and zero eigenvalues a degenerate case requiring additional information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local type is recorded by the neighborhood-order relation together with \(\operatorname{In}(\nabla^2f(x_*))=(n_+,n_-,n_0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: An indefinite symmetric Hessian is equivalent to \(n_+>0\) and \(n_->0\).
Hessian nondegeneracy is equivalent to \(n_0=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \((n_+,n_-,n_0)=(n,0,0)\), the point is a strict isolated local minimum.
If \((n_+,n_-,n_0)=(0,n,0)\), the point is a strict isolated local maximum.
immediate_consequences_latex: A mixed-sign Hessian excludes both local minimality and local maximality.
A singular semidefinite Hessian does not uniquely determine the local point type.
boundary_notes: The taxonomy is local and does not identify global extrema.
Nonisolated stationary sets and degenerate saddles require information beyond Hessian inertia.

notation.meaning: Numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of the Hessian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical Local Types of a Smooth Critical Point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable near \(x_*\) and suppose \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood-order classification of smooth unconstrained critical points, with standard Hessian refinements when \(f\in C^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A critical point \(x_*\) is a local minimum if some \(r>0\) satisfies \(f(x_*)\le f(x)\) for \(\|x-x_*\|<r\), and a strict local minimum if the inequality is strict whenever \(0<\|x-x_*\|<r\). Local and strict local maxima are defined by reversing these inequalities. A saddle point has arbitrarily close points on both sides of its value: for every \(r>0\), there exist \(y,z\) with \(\|y-x_*\|,\|z-x_*\|<r\) and \(f(y)<f(x_*)<f(z)\). A critical point not decided by these strict alternatives is degenerate or nonisolated according to its higher-order or stationary-set geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical taxonomy classifies a critical point by comparing its objective value with all sufficiently nearby values. It distinguishes local minima, strict local minima, local maxima, strict local maxima, and saddles. Hessian definiteness supplies familiar sufficient classifications, while singular cases may remain degenerate or belong to a nonisolated stationary set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly specified neighborhood inequalities define the minimum, maximum, and saddle labels at \(x_*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(f\in C^2\), \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\) implies a strict isolated local minimum, and \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\prec0\) implies a strict isolated local maximum.
For \(f\in C^2\), an indefinite Hessian implies the saddle neighborhood-order condition.
special_cases_latex: A nonstrict local minimum may lie on a continuum of equal-valued local minima.
A critical point with positive-semidefinite singular Hessian can be a minimum or a nonminimum degenerate point.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strict local minima and strict local maxima are isolated as extrema in a sufficiently small punctured neighborhood.
A saddle is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum.
boundary_notes: The word degenerate is spectral or higher-order terminology and is not itself a complete neighborhood-order type.
The definitions do not assert that every critical point is isolated.

children.title: Strict Local Minima
children.top_down_role: Isolated locally minimizing stationary points.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Local Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard strict local-minimizer notion in a metric domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(x_*\in X\). The point \(x_*\) is a strict local minimizer if there exists \(r>0\) such that
\[f(x)>f(x_*)\quad\text{for every }x\in X\text{ with }0<\|x-x_*\|<r.\]
If \(X\) contains a neighborhood of \(x_*\) and \(f\) is differentiable there, strict local minimality implies \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\). Strictness isolates \(x_*\) among local competitors having no larger objective value, but does not by itself imply quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict local minimizer has strictly smaller objective value than every other sufficiently nearby feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(r>0\) such that \(0<\|x-x_*\|<r\) and \(x\in X\) imply \(f(x)>f(x_*)\).

notation.meaning: Open Euclidean ball of radius r centered at x_*.

children.title: Nonstrict Local Minima
children.top_down_role: Local minima accompanied by flat or nonisolated directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonstrict Local Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained finite-dimensional definition emphasizing equality arbitrarily close to the minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\). A point \(x_\star\in U\) is a nonstrict local minimum if there exists \(r>0\) such that \(f(x)\geq f(x_\star)\) whenever \(x\in U\) and \(\lVert x-x_\star\rVert<r\), but \(x_\star\) is not a strict local minimum. Equivalently, for every \(0<\rho<r\), there exists \(x_\rho\in U\) with \(0<\lVert x_\rho-x_\star\rVert<\rho\) and \(f(x_\rho)=f(x_\star)\). If \(f\) is differentiable, then \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonstrict local minimum minimizes nearby values, but distinct points with the same objective value occur arbitrarily close to it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\star\) is locally minimizing but not strictly locally minimizing.

notation.meaning: Open radius-r ball centered at the candidate point.
A distinct nearby point attaining the same objective value.

children.top_down_role: Stationary points locally unfavorable for minimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Maxima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior unconstrained local maxima, including the first- and second-order consequences of smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\). A point \(x_\star\in U\) is a local maximum if some \(r>0\) satisfies \(f(x)\leq f(x_\star)\) for every \(x\in U\) with \(\lVert x-x_\star\rVert<r\). If \(f\) is differentiable at \(x_\star\), then \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\). If \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(x_\star\), then \(d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2 f(x_\star)d\leq0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local maximum dominates all sufficiently nearby objective values; at a smooth interior point its gradient vanishes and its Hessian is negative semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\leq f(x_\star)\) throughout some neighborhood of \(x_\star\).

notation.meaning: Hessian of the objective at the local maximum.
An arbitrary direction in the ambient space.

children.title: Strict Saddles

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the classical indefinite-Hessian sense, separating strict saddles from local maxima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A critical point \(x_\star\in U\) is a strict saddle if \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\) and its Hessian \(H_\star=\nabla^2f(x_\star)\) has both signs of curvature: there exist nonzero directions \(d_-\) and \(d_+\) such that \(d_-^{\mathsf T}H_\star d_-<0<d_+^{\mathsf T}H_\star d_+\). Equivalently, \(\lambda_{\min}(H_\star)<0<\lambda_{\max}(H_\star)\). Consequently, arbitrarily near \(x_\star\), the objective takes values both below and above \(f(x_\star)\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x_\star))<0<\lambda_{\max}(\nabla^2f(x_\star))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical saddle points whose Hessian is singular, so quadratic curvature does not fully resolve the local geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A critical point \(x_\star\in U\) is a degenerate saddle if \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\), the Hessian \(H_\star=\nabla^2f(x_\star)\) is singular, and every neighborhood \(V\subseteq U\) of \(x_\star\) contains points \(x^-\) and \(x^+\) satisfying \(f(x^-)<f(x_\star)<f(x^+)\). Thus \(x_\star\) is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum, while at least one Hessian-null direction prevents a nondegenerate quadratic classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate saddle has nearby values on both sides of its critical value and a singular Hessian, leaving some directions unresolved at second order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det\nabla^2f(x_\star)=0\), with both ascent and descent values arbitrarily near \(x_\star\).

notation.meaning: Nearby points with lower and higher objective values.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\) at \(x\), and set \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Euclidean local curvature represented by the eigenspaces and inertia of a real symmetric Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an orthogonal eigendecomposition \[H=U\Lambda U^\top,\qquad \Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n).\] The positive, negative, and null curvature subspaces are \[E_+=\operatorname{span}\{u_i:\lambda_i>0\},\quad E_-=\operatorname{span}\{u_i:\lambda_i<0\},\quad E_0=\ker H.\] The spectral curvature geometry of \(f\) at \(x\) is the orthogonal decomposition \(\mathbb R^n=E_+\oplus E_-\oplus E_0\), together with the eigenvalues on these subspaces, the extremal curvatures \(\lambda_{\min}(H),\lambda_{\max}(H)\), and the inertia \((\dim E_+,\dim E_-,\dim E_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric Hessian has an orthonormal eigenbasis. Eigenvectors with positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues span mutually orthogonal subspaces describing locally upward, downward, and quadratically unresolved directions. The eigenvalues, extremal eigenvalues, and dimensions of these subspaces constitute the local spectral curvature geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\) is represented in the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R^n=E_+\oplus E_-\oplus E_0\) orthogonally, and \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(\dim E_+,\dim E_-,\dim E_0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(d=d_++d_-+d_0\) in the three subspaces, \(d^\top Hd=d_+^\top Hd_++d_-^\top Hd_-\), with positive, negative, and zero signs respectively.
\(H\succeq0\iff E_-=\{0\}\), and \(H\succ0\iff E_-=E_0=\{0\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H=0\), then \(E_0=\mathbb R^n\) and second-order curvature is entirely unresolved.
If \(H\) is indefinite, both \(E_+\) and \(E_-\) are nontrivial.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every negative-curvature direction has a nonzero component in \(E_-\).
Hessian singularity is equivalent to \(E_0\ne\{0\}\).
boundary_notes: Eigenvectors inside a repeated-eigenvalue subspace are not unique, but the invariant subspace is unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian Inertia, Morse Index, Coindex, and Nullity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be a real symmetric matrix, in particular \(H=\nabla^2f(x_*)\) at a \(C^2\) critical point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional spectral classification of local quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the inertia of \(H\) by \[\operatorname{In}(H)=(n_+,n_-,n_0),\] where \(n_+\), \(n_-\), and \(n_0\) are the eigenvalue counts, including multiplicity, in \((0,\infty)\), \(( -\infty,0)\), and \(\{0\}\), respectively. The Morse index is \(\operatorname{ind}(H):=n_-\), the coindex is \(\operatorname{coind}(H):=n_+\), and the nullity is \(\operatorname{nul}(H):=n_0=\dim\ker H\). Hence \(n_++n_-+n_0=n\), and these integers equal the dimensions of the positive-, negative-, and zero-curvature invariant subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inertia of a symmetric Hessian counts its positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues. The negative count is its Morse index, the positive count its coindex, and the zero count its nullity. These counts are exactly the dimensions of the corresponding curvature subspaces and sum to the ambient dimension.
assumptions_latex: Eigenvalues are counted with algebraic multiplicity, which equals geometric multiplicity for a real symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(\operatorname{coind}(H),\operatorname{ind}(H),\operatorname{nul}(H))\) and their sum is \(n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{ind}(H)=\dim E_-\), \(\operatorname{coind}(H)=\dim E_+\), and \(\operatorname{nul}(H)=\dim E_0\).
special_cases_latex: \(H\succ0\iff\operatorname{In}(H)=(n,0,0)\).
\(H\prec0\iff\operatorname{In}(H)=(0,n,0)\).
\(H\) is nonsingular and indefinite when \(n_+>0\), \(n_->0\), and \(n_0=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A critical point is Hessian-nondegenerate exactly when \(\operatorname{nul}(H)=0\).
A positive Morse index records the existence of negative quadratic curvature.
boundary_notes: The inertia is basis-independent under orthogonal changes of coordinates.
The Morse index does not by itself classify a degenerate point when the nullity is positive.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral signature of a real symmetric Hessian in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a twice differentiable function \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) and a point \(x\in U\), let \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\). Because \(H\) is real symmetric, all its eigenvalues are real. Its inertia signature is the triple \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(n_+(H),n_-(H),n_0(H))\), where \(n_+(H)\), \(n_-(H)\), and \(n_0(H)\) count, with algebraic multiplicity, the positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of \(H\), respectively. knowledge_statements.title: Inertia-to-Index Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Morse-lemma correspondence for nondegenerate critical points in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(x_\star\in U\) be a nondegenerate critical point. If \(\operatorname{In}(\nabla^2f(x_\star))=(n_+,n_-,0)\), then the Morse index of \(x_\star\) is \(n_-\). Moreover, there are local coordinates \(y\) centered at \(x_\star\) in which \(f(x)-f(x_\star)=-\sum_{i=1}^{n_-}y_i^2+\sum_{i=n_-+1}^{n}y_i^2\). Hence index \(0\) characterizes a strict local minimum, index \(n\) a strict local maximum, and an index strictly between \(0\) and \(n\) a saddle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nondegenerate critical point, the number of negative Hessian eigenvalues equals its Morse index and determines minimum, maximum, or saddle type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{ind}(x_\star)=n_-(\nabla^2f(x_\star))\), with the stated local quadratic normal form.

notation.meaning: Number of negative Hessian eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Hessian Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies singular Hessians as the only boundaries across which spectral inertia can change continuously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:[0,1]\to\mathbb{S}^n\) be continuous. On every connected interval \(I\subseteq[0,1]\) for which \(\det H(t)\neq0\), the inertia counts \(n_+(H(t))\) and \(n_-(H(t))\) are constant. Therefore, if two parameters \(s,t\) have different inertia signatures, some \(\tau\) between them satisfies \(\det H(\tau)=0\). Applied to \(H(t)=\nabla^2f(x(t))\), a change in critical-point index along a continuous branch can occur only at a singular Hessian. At such a boundary, the quadratic model has a nontrivial nullspace and cannot alone classify behavior in those null directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian inertia is locally constant while the Hessian is nonsingular; any change of critical-point index must pass through a zero eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{In}(H(t))\) is constant on \(I\), and an inertia change requires \(n_0(H(\tau))>0\).

notation.meaning: Space of real symmetric n-by-n matrices.
A parameter at which an eigenvalue reaches zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hessian Null Space and Quadratically Flat Directions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable at \(x\), and let \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth local geometry of directions on which the Hessian supplies no quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Hessian-null subspace at \(x\) is \[N_x:=\ker H=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Hd=0\}.\] Its dimension \(\nu_x:=\dim N_x\) is the Hessian nullity. For a positive-semidefinite Hessian, every direction with zero quadratic form lies in this kernel. Higher derivatives or variation transverse to the point are needed to classify behavior along these directions.

children.title: Second-Order Indeterminacy
children.top_down_role: Classification limits caused by vanishing Hessian curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Indeterminacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a singular positive-semidefinite Hessian to classify a stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x_\star\), with \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\) and \(H=\nabla^2 f(x_\star)\succeq0\). If \(H\) is singular, then for every nonzero \(v\in\ker H\), Taylor expansion gives \[f(x_\star+t v)=f(x_\star)+o(t^2)\quad\text{as }t\to0.\] Thus the gradient and Hessian do not determine whether \(f\) increases, decreases, or remains constant along \(v\). In particular, second-order necessary conditions alone cannot distinguish a degenerate local minimum from a degenerate saddle or a locally flat critical set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a stationary point with a singular positive-semidefinite Hessian, null directions have no quadratic variation, so second-order data alone cannot classify the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\star\) is not classifiable from second-order information alone.

children.title: Spectral Separation-Conditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Separation and sensitivity of stable, unstable, and flat modes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral separation and conditioning at a critical point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(x_\star\in U\) satisfy \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\), and write \(H_\star=\nabla^2f(x_\star)\). Denote the negative, zero, and positive spectral subspaces of the symmetric matrix \(H_\star\) by \(E_-\), \(E_0\), and \(E_+\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, unconstrained, twice-smooth local geometry at one critical point. The definition separates stable, unstable, and flat Hessian modes and records conditioning only on nonzero spectral subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constants \(\alpha_-,\alpha_+>0\) and \(L\geq\max\{\alpha_-,\alpha_+\}\), the critical point \(x_\star\) is in the spectral separation-conditioning regime \((\alpha_-,\alpha_+,L)\) if \(\sigma(H_\star)\subseteq[-L,-\alpha_-]\cup\{0\}\cup[\alpha_+,L]\). Its negative and positive restricted condition numbers are \(\kappa_-=\lambda_{\max}(-H_\star|_{E_-})/\lambda_{\min}(-H_\star|_{E_-})\) and \(\kappa_+=\lambda_{\max}(H_\star|_{E_+})/\lambda_{\min}(H_\star|_{E_+})\), with the corresponding quantity left undefined when its subspace is trivial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A critical point belongs to a spectral separation-conditioning regime when every negative Hessian eigenvalue is bounded away from zero by a prescribed negative gap, every positive eigenvalue is bounded away from zero by a prescribed positive gap, and all nonzero eigenvalues have bounded magnitude. Conditioning is measured separately on the unstable and stable spectral subspaces; zero eigenvalues form the flat subspace and are not included in either condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sigma(H_\star)\subseteq[-L,-\alpha_-]\cup\{0\}\cup[\alpha_+,L],\qquad \mathbb R^n=E_-\oplus E_0\oplus E_+.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The separation condition is equivalent to \(-H_\star|_{E_-}\succeq\alpha_-I\), \(H_\star|_{E_+}\succeq\alpha_+I\), and \(\|H_\star\|_2\leq L\).
special_cases_latex: If \(E_0=\{0\}\), then \(H_\star\) is nonsingular and the critical point is nondegenerate.
If \(E_-=\{0\}\) and \(E_0=\{0\}\), then \(H_\star\succeq\alpha_+I\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The inertia \((\dim E_-,\dim E_0,\dim E_+)\) is stable under symmetric perturbations of operator norm smaller than \(\min\{\alpha_-,\alpha_+\}\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not classify behavior along the flat subspace; higher-order terms may determine whether flat directions are minimizing, maximizing, or saddle-like.
Restricted condition numbers are not assigned the artificial value one on a zero-dimensional spectral subspace.

notation.meaning: Negative, null, and positive spectral subspaces of the Hessian.
Spectral gaps separating nonzero eigenvalues from zero.
Condition numbers of the negative and positive Hessian restrictions.

children.title: Spectral Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Separation regimes among stable, unstable, and nearly flat curvature modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of a Hessian eigenvalue cluster from its spectral complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, with ordered eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n\), and let \(I\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be nonempty. Define the cluster gap by \[\delta_I(H)=\min_{i\in I,\,j\notin I}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|.\] The cluster is spectrally separated precisely when \(\delta_I(H)>0\); it is nonseparated when \(\delta_I(H)=0\). Relative to a perturbation scale \(\eta\geq0\), the regimes \(\delta_I(H)>2\eta\), \(0<\delta_I(H)\leq2\eta\), and \(\delta_I(H)=0\) are respectively robustly separated, weakly separated, and degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian mode cluster is isolated when its eigenvalues have positive distance from the remaining spectrum; comparison with perturbation size determines robustness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_I(H)\) classifies the cluster as robustly separated, weakly separated, or degenerate at scale \(\eta\).

notation.meaning: index set of the selected spectral cluster
distance from the cluster to the complementary spectrum

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and positive-gap definition fit Spectral Gap Regimes. However, no source is cited for the scale-dependent labels or the particular threshold 2η; these are conventions rather than consequences of the definition and require an authoritative spectral-perturbation locator.

children.title: Curvature Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning of local curvature classification under spectral scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of nonzero Hessian curvature on a selected invariant subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonzero \(H\)-invariant subspace. If the restriction \(H|_S\) is nonsingular, define its absolute curvature condition number by \[\kappa_S(H)=\frac{\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(H|_S)\}}{\min\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(H|_S)\}}.\] If \(H|_S\) is singular, set \(\kappa_S(H)=+\infty\). Finite values near \(1\) represent uniformly scaled curvature, whereas large values indicate disparate curvature scales and amplification by the inverse restricted Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature conditioning is the ratio of largest to smallest nonzero absolute Hessian curvature on an invariant subspace, with singular restrictions assigned infinite conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_S(H)\in[1,+\infty]\) quantifies the disparity of curvature magnitudes on \(S\).

notation.meaning: restriction of the Hessian to the invariant subspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Curvature Conditioning, and the displayed ratio is mathematically coherent for a nonzero invariant subspace. An authoritative locator is required for calling this quantity the absolute curvature condition number and for the inverse-amplification interpretation.

children.title: Eigenspace Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of curvature modes to perturbations in local derivative information.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenspace Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric eigenspace perturbation bound for an isolated cluster.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H,\widetilde H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and write \(E=\widetilde H-H\). Suppose a spectral cluster of \(H\) is separated from the complementary spectrum by \(\delta>0\), and let \(P\) be its orthogonal spectral projector. If \(\|E\|_2<\delta/2\), the corresponding cluster of \(\widetilde H\) has the same dimension and an orthogonal projector \(\widetilde P\) satisfying \[\|\widetilde P-P\|_2\leq\frac{2\|E\|_2}{\delta}.\] Hence eigenspace sensitivity grows inversely with the spectral gap, while individual eigenvectors inside a repeated cluster need not be uniquely stable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isolated symmetric-Hessian eigenspace changes by at most a constant times perturbation size divided by its spectral gap; vectors within repeated clusters may rotate.
assumptions_latex: The selected cluster of \(H\) has gap \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde P-P\|_2\leq2\|\widetilde H-H\|_2/\delta\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal projectors onto corresponding spectral clusters

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits Eigenspace Sensitivity, but the exact projector constant and gap convention require a Davis–Kahan or equivalent theorem locator. The selected cluster and its corresponding perturbed cluster also need a precise spectral-set correspondence, especially when the selected index set is not a contiguous cluster.

children.title: Mode-Separation Reliability
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits for distinguishing stable, unstable, or flat modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Mode-Separation Reliability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certification that an observed Hessian eigenvalue split survives bounded error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be an unknown symmetric Hessian and let \(\widehat H\) be symmetric with a certified error bound \(\|\widehat H-H\|_2\leq\eta\). Order both spectra increasingly and define the observed split \(\widehat g_k=\lambda_{k+1}(\widehat H)-\lambda_k(\widehat H)\). If \(\widehat g_k>2\eta\), then Weyl perturbation bounds imply \[\lambda_{k+1}(H)-\lambda_k(H)\geq\widehat g_k-2\eta>0.\] Thus \((\widehat H,\eta,\widehat g_k)\) certifies a true separation after the first \(k\) modes and prevents eigenvalue-order exchange across that split under every admissible Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Hessian gap exceeding twice the certified spectral-norm error proves that the corresponding true mode split is positive and cannot exchange order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{k+1}(H)-\lambda_k(H)\geq\widehat g_k-2\eta>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the terminal container, and Weyl bounds support the displayed lower bound on the true adjacent gap. A specific source is still required. Moreover, positivity of the ordered true gap certifies separation but does not by itself identify individual eigenmodes across matrices, so the claim about preventing mode or eigenvalue-order exchange needs precise qualification.

children.title: Morse-Type Local Geometry Family
children.top_down_role: Classical local organization of nondegenerate critical points and structured critical manifolds.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb R\) a \(C^2\) function. Its critical set is \(\operatorname{Crit}(f)=\{x\in M:df_x=0\}\). At a critical point, the Hessian \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\) is an intrinsic symmetric bilinear form on \(T_xM\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth local geometry. The family contains isolated Morse points and Morse–Bott critical submanifolds, but excludes more singular critical sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A connected component \(C\subseteq\operatorname{Crit}(f)\) has Morse-type local geometry if \(C\) is an embedded submanifold and, for every \(x\in C\), \(\ker(\operatorname{Hess}f(x))=T_xC\). The isolated case \(C=\{x_\star\}\) is therefore Morse precisely when \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)\) is nonsingular; the positive-dimensional case is Morse–Bott. The index is \(\operatorname{ind}(C)=\dim E_-(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)|_{N_xC})\), which is constant on connected \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A critical component has Morse-type geometry when it is a smooth embedded manifold and the only Hessian-null directions are those tangent to that component. An isolated component is a Morse critical point; a positive-dimensional component is Morse–Bott. The number of negative transverse Hessian directions is its index and is constant along a connected component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C\subseteq\operatorname{Crit}(f),\qquad C\text{ embedded},\qquad \ker(\operatorname{Hess}f(x))=T_xC\quad(\forall x\in C).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any complement \(N_xC\) of \(T_xC\), the induced Hessian form on the normal quotient \(T_xM/T_xC\) is nondegenerate.
When \(C=\{x_\star\}\), the defining kernel equality is equivalent to \(\det\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)\neq0\).
special_cases_latex: A zero-dimensional component gives classical Morse geometry.
A positive-dimensional component gives Morse–Bott geometry with nondegenerate transverse curvature.
immediate_consequences_latex: The transverse positive and negative inertia are locally constant on \(C\), hence constant when \(C\) is connected.
The definition separates symmetry-induced tangent flatness from additional degeneracy transverse to the critical component.
boundary_notes: A stationary manifold whose Hessian has extra normal null directions is not Morse-type under this definition.
A nonmanifold critical set, including a crossing of smooth critical strata, is excluded even if individual strata have nondegenerate transverse Hessians.

notation.meaning: Connected embedded component of the critical set.
A chosen normal complement to the tangent space of the critical component.
Number of negative transverse Hessian eigenvalues.

children.title: Morse Critical Points
children.top_down_role: Isolated nondegenerate critical points organized by curvature index.

knowledge_statements.title: Morse Critical Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate smooth critical points classified by Hessian index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a smooth \(n\)-dimensional manifold and let \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be smooth. A point \(p\in M\) is a Morse critical point when \(df_p=0\) and the Hessian bilinear form \(\operatorname{Hess}_p f:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb{R}\) is nondegenerate. Its Morse index \(\mu(p)\) is the number of negative eigenvalues of any matrix representing \(\operatorname{Hess}_p f\), counted with multiplicity. Nondegeneracy makes \(p\) isolated among critical points; indices \(0\), \(n\), and \(1,\ldots,n-1\) correspond locally to minima, maxima, and saddles, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Morse critical point has zero differential and nonsingular Hessian; its index counts negative Hessian eigenvalues and determines its local curvature type.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth manifold of dimension \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is Morse exactly when \(df_p=0\) and \(\operatorname{Hess}_p f\) is nondegenerate.

notation.meaning: tangent space of the manifold at the critical point
Morse index of the critical point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Morse critical point and Morse index
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional smooth manifold, let \(f:M\to\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\), and let \(x_\star\in M\). At a critical point \(df_{x_\star}=0\), the Hessian is a coordinate-independent symmetric bilinear form on \(T_{x_\star}M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, twice-smooth, unconstrained local critical-point geometry. The definition concerns an individual critical point rather than a critical manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(x_\star\) is a Morse critical point of \(f\) if \(df_{x_\star}=0\) and \(\ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)=\{0\}\). Its Morse index \(\lambda(x_\star)\) is the maximal dimension of a subspace of \(T_{x_\star}M\) on which the Hessian is negative definite, equivalently the number of negative Hessian eigenvalues counted with multiplicity in any local coordinate representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Morse critical point is a stationary point with a nonsingular Hessian. Its Morse index is the number of independent negative-curvature directions, counted with multiplicity. Index zero identifies a strict local-minimum type, index equal to the manifold dimension identifies a strict local-maximum type, and intermediate index identifies a saddle type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[df_{x_\star}=0,\qquad \ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)=\{0\},\qquad \lambda(x_\star)=n_-(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)).\]

If \(0<\lambda(x_\star)<n\), the Hessian is indefinite and \(x_\star\) has saddle type.
If \(\lambda(x_\star)=n\), the Hessian is negative definite and \(x_\star\) has strict local-maximum type.
immediate_consequences_latex: A Morse critical point is isolated in the critical set.
Its inertia is unchanged by sufficiently small \(C^2\) perturbations that preserve a nearby critical point.

children.title: Morse Lemma Family
children.top_down_role: Local normal-form principles for nondegenerate critical points.

knowledge_statements.title: Morse Lemma Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth local quadratic normal form at a nondegenerate critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a smooth \(n\)-manifold, let \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be smooth, and let \(p\) be a Morse critical point of index \(\mu\). Then there is a smooth coordinate chart \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)\) centered at \(p\) such that, throughout a neighborhood of \(p\), \[f(y)=f(p)-\sum_{i=1}^{\mu}y_i^2+\sum_{i=\mu+1}^{n}y_i^2.\] Consequently, the local germ of \(f\) at \(p\), up to a smooth change of coordinates, is determined by the critical value, dimension, and Morse index; no terms of order three or higher remain in these coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nondegenerate critical point, smooth coordinates transform the function exactly into a signed sum of squares whose negative count is the Morse index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) admits the displayed signed-quadratic local normal form near \(p\).

notation.meaning: local coordinates centered at the critical point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind correctly fits the Morse Lemma Family, and the smooth signed-quadratic normal form is stated with appropriate hypotheses. A specific authoritative Morse lemma theorem or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional smooth manifold, let \(f:M\to\mathbb R\), and let \(x_\star\) be a critical point. Fix an integer \(0\leq\lambda\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local normal-form property near an isolated nondegenerate critical point. This definition records the geometry characterized by the classical Morse lemma without asserting or proving the lemma itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The germ of \(f\) at \(x_\star\) has Morse normal form of index \(\lambda\) if there exist a neighborhood \(V\) of \(x_\star\), a neighborhood \(W\) of \(0\in\mathbb R^n\), and a local diffeomorphism \(\psi:V\to W\) with \(\psi(x_\star)=0\) such that, for every \(x\in V\), \[f(x)=f(x_\star)-\sum_{i=1}^{\lambda}\psi_i(x)^2+\sum_{i=\lambda+1}^{n}\psi_i(x)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function has Morse normal-form geometry at a critical point when a smooth local change of coordinates removes all terms beyond a diagonal quadratic form with a fixed number of negative squares. That number is the index. The normal form is exact on a neighborhood, not merely a second-order Taylor approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f\circ\psi^{-1}(y)=f(x_\star)-\|y_{1:\lambda}\|^2+\|y_{\lambda+1:n}\|^2\quad\text{for all }y\in W.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: After an invertible linear rescaling of the normal coordinates, the coefficients of all nonzero quadratic terms may be written as \(+1\) or \(-1\).
The index equals the negative inertia of the Hessian at \(x_\star\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\lambda=0\), the normal form is \(f(x_\star)+\|y\|^2\).
For \(\lambda=n\), the normal form is \(f(x_\star)-\|y\|^2\).
For \(0<\lambda<n\), the normal form contains both ascent and descent directions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The critical point is isolated within the normal-form neighborhood.
The local critical-point type is determined completely by the index.
boundary_notes: The exact differentiability threshold needed to obtain a particular regularity class of coordinate change is not fixed here; the coordinate map and objective must be taken sufficiently smooth for the asserted local diffeomorphism.
Degenerate points and Morse–Bott critical manifolds require different normal forms.

notation.meaning: Local coordinate diffeomorphism placing the objective in quadratic normal form.
Number of negative squares in the normal form.

children.title: Morse–Bott Critical Manifolds
children.top_down_role: Nonisolated critical manifolds with controlled transverse curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Morse–Bott Critical Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical submanifolds whose only Hessian-null directions are tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a smooth manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) smooth. An embedded submanifold \(C\subset M\) is a Morse–Bott critical manifold of \(f\) when \(C\subset\operatorname{Crit}(f)\) and, for every \(p\in C\), \[\ker\bigl(\operatorname{Hess}_p f:T_pM\to T_p^*M\bigr)=T_pC.\] Equivalently, the Hessian induces a nondegenerate quadratic form on the normal quotient \(T_pM/T_pC\). Thus degeneracy is permitted exactly along the critical manifold, while all transverse directions possess nonzero quadratic curvature; the transverse index is locally constant on each connected component of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Morse–Bott critical manifold consists of critical points whose Hessian kernel equals the manifold’s tangent space, leaving nondegenerate curvature in every transverse direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is Morse–Bott precisely when \(C\subset\operatorname{Crit}(f)\) and \(\ker\operatorname{Hess}_p f=T_pC\) for every \(p\in C\).

notation.meaning: tangent space of the critical manifold
normal quotient at the critical point

Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable. The function has the qualitative strict-saddle property when every critical point \(x\), meaning \(

children.title: Robust Strict-Saddle Property

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Strict-Saddle Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative trichotomy among large gradient, negative curvature, and strongly convex minimizer neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable and let \(\mathcal M\) be its set of local minimizers. For constants \(\varepsilon,\gamma,\delta,\alpha>0\), call \(f\) robustly strict-saddle if every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies at least one of \[\|
abla f(x)\|\geq\varepsilon,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\leq-\gamma,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal M)\leq\delta,\] and the final alternative entails \(
abla^2f(y)\succeq\alpha I\) for every \(y\) in the relevant \(2\delta\)-neighborhood of its associated minimizer. This supplies uniform margins absent from the qualitative property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point has either a large gradient, uniformly negative curvature, or proximity to a minimizer with a uniformly strongly convex neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: Local minimizers in \(\mathcal M\) are isolated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed gradient–curvature–minimizer trichotomy holds uniformly over \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Robust Strict-Saddle Property, but quantitative definitions vary. The phrase 'associated minimizer' is not defined, and the stated 2δ strong-convexity neighborhood is not tied unambiguously to the distance alternative. An authoritative formulation and locator are necessary before the exact hypotheses can be fixed.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\) on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(X_{\min}\subseteq U\) be a nonempty closed set of accepted local minimizers. Let \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X_{\min})=\inf_{z\in X_{\min}}\|x-z\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative finite-dimensional condition for approximate stationarity. This formulation includes local uniform positive curvature near the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\epsilon,\gamma,\delta,\mu>0\), the function \(f\) is \((\epsilon,\gamma,\delta,\mu)\)-robust strict saddle relative to \(X_{\min}\) if every \(x\in U\) satisfies at least one of \[\|
abla f(x)\|\geq\epsilon,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\leq-\gamma,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x,X_{\min})\leq\delta,\] and, throughout the minimizer tube, \[\operatorname{dist}(x,X_{\min})\leq2\delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v^	op
abla^2f(x)v\geq\mu\|v\|^2\] for every displacement direction \(v=x-P_{X_{\min}}(x)\) associated with a chosen nearest minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust strict-saddle landscape quantitatively partitions every point into a large-gradient region, a uniformly negative-curvature region, or a fixed neighborhood of accepted minimizers. In an enlarged minimizer neighborhood, the objective must also have uniform positive curvature along displacement directions leading away from the nearest minimizer set. For isolated minimizers this clause may be strengthened to full strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad \|\nabla f(x)\|\geq\epsilon\ \lor\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\leq-\gamma\ \lor\ \operatorname{dist}(x,X_{\min})\leq\delta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The three-region clause is equivalent to requiring \(\|\nabla f(x)\|<\epsilon\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))> -\gamma\) only inside the \(\delta\)-tube around \(X_{\min}\).
special_cases_latex: For isolated minimizers, one may impose \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I\) on each \(2\delta\)-ball.
For minimizer manifolds, positive curvature is naturally required only in normal displacement directions because tangent directions may be flat.

Every approximate second-order stationary point satisfying \(\|\nabla f(x)\|<\epsilon\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))> -\gamma\) lies within distance \(\delta\) of \(X_{\min}\).
boundary_notes: Definitions in the literature differ in the minimizer-neighborhood clause, its radius, and whether full strong convexity or directional regularity is required.
Nearest-point projections need not be unique for a general closed set; the directional clause must hold for each projection selected by the adopted convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Ridable-Saddle Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict saddles equipped with an efficiently discoverable negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable, and fix \(\gamma>0\). Relative to a specified Hessian-vector oracle and resource bound \(T\), the saddles of \(f\) are ridable if every critical point \(x\) that is not a local minimizer satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\leq-\gamma\), and the oracle procedure returns within \(T\) operations a unit vector \(v\) such that \[v^\top\nabla^2f(x)v\leq-\gamma/2.\] The vector is a computationally accessible descent direction for the local quadratic model, rather than merely an existential unstable mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonminimal critical point has uniformly negative curvature, and a specified oracle can find a comparably negative unit direction within the stated resource bound.
assumptions_latex: A Hessian-vector oracle and resource bound \(T\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A unit direction \(v\) with \(v^\top\nabla^2f(x)v\leq-\gamma/2\) is computable within \(T\) operations at every nonminimal critical point.

notation.meaning: resource bound for finding the unstable direction

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\) on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f_\star=\inf_{x\in U}f(x)\), and let \(X_\star=\{x\in U:f(x)=f_\star\}\) be nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Application-facing finite-dimensional landscape definition coupling saddle instability with absence of spurious local minima and quantitative local regularity near global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has an \((\epsilon,\gamma,\delta,\mu)\)-favorable strict-saddle coupling if: (i) every local minimizer belongs to \(X_\star\); (ii) every \(x\in U\) satisfies \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\geq\epsilon\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\leq-\gamma\), or \(\operatorname{dist}(x,X_\star)\leq\delta\); and (iii) for every \(x_\star\in X_\star\), the local growth inequality \(f(x)-f_\star\geq(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,X_\star)^2\) holds whenever \(\|x-x_\star\|\leq2\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A favorable strict-saddle landscape combines three features: all local minima are globally optimal, points away from global minimizers have either a large gradient or uniform negative curvature, and the objective grows at least quadratically with distance from the global-minimizer set in a local neighborhood. This couples global landscape classification with local recoverability around desired solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{LocMin}(f)\subseteq X_\star,\qquad U\subseteq\{\|\nabla f\|\geq\epsilon\}\cup\{\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f)\leq-\gamma\}\cup\{\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,X_\star)\leq\delta\}.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(X_\star=\{x_\star\}\), the local growth clause is ordinary quadratic growth around an isolated global minimizer.
For symmetry-related minimizers forming a manifold, growth is measured by distance to the entire equivalence class rather than to one representative.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every approximate second-order stationary point lies near a global minimizer.
No spurious local minimum is permitted.
The local growth clause converts parameter distance to an objective-value error bound near \(X_\star\).
boundary_notes: Quadratic growth is weaker than full strong convexity and accommodates flat tangent directions along a minimizer manifold.
The definition does not imply uniqueness of a global minimizer.
Constants and the chosen local regularity condition are application-dependent and are not canonical across the literature.

children.title: Strict-Saddle Structure

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Saddle Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of the critical set into local minima and unstable saddle strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable and let \(\operatorname{Crit}(f)=\{x:\nabla f(x)=0\}\). A strict-saddle structure is a decomposition \[\operatorname{Crit}(f)=\mathcal M\,\dot\cup\,\mathcal S,\] where every point of \(\mathcal M\) is a local minimizer and every \(x\in\mathcal S\) satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))<0\). Consequently, every nonminimal critical component possesses an unstable normal direction, and no critical point can be a nonminimal local maximum, a degenerate saddle without negative curvature, or a higher-order saddle whose Hessian is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical set splits into local minima and saddles with a strictly negative Hessian eigenvalue, excluding flat nonminimal stationary points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Crit}(f)=\mathcal M\dot\cup\mathcal S\) with \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))<0\) for every \(x\in\mathcal S\).

notation.meaning: local-minimizer portion of the critical set
strict-saddle portion of the critical set

The assumption '\(fin C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\)' is malformed and should read '\(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\)'. The assertion excluding nonminimal local maxima is false under the displayed decomposition: a nondegenerate local maximum has a negative Hessian eigenvalue and can belong to S. A sourced formulation is needed before producing a reliable replacement.

children.title: Absence of Spurious Minima

knowledge_statements.title: Absence of Spurious Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global benignity of local minima for an unconstrained smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\). The landscape of \(f\) has no spurious local minima when every local minimizer is globally minimizing: for every \(x_\star\in\mathbb{R}^n\), if there exists \(r>0\) such that \(f(x_\star)\leq f(x)\) whenever \(\|x-x_\star\|<r\), then \(f(x_\star)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)\). This property permits multiple or nonisolated global minimizers and does not, by itself, restrict nonminimizing stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No local minimum is spurious: every point minimizing the objective in some neighborhood also attains its global infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathrm{loc}} f\subseteq\operatorname{argmin} f\).

notation.meaning: set of local minimizers of the objective
set of global minimizers of the objective

knowledge_statements.title: Favorable Landscape Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Couples global optimality of minima with negative curvature at every other critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A twice continuously differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) has the favorable strict-saddle coupling when every critical point \(x\) satisfies exactly one of the following alternatives: \(x\in\operatorname{argmin}f\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 f(x))<0\). Consequently, every local minimizer is global, while every nonglobal critical point possesses a direction \(v
eq0\) with \(v^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(x)v<0\). Degenerate nonglobal critical points with positive-semidefinite Hessian are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every critical point is either a global minimizer or has a direction of strictly negative curvature; hence spurious minima and flat nonglobal critical points are absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f(x)=0\Longrightarrow x\in\operatorname{argmin}f\ \lor\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))<0\).

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Property Landscapes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates absence of spurious local minima from the stronger negative-curvature condition at every nonglobal critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\), define \(P_{\mathrm{min}}\) by \(\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathrm{loc}}f\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}f\), and define \(P_{\mathrm{ss}}\) by requiring \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))<0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(
abla f(x)=0\) and \(x
otin\operatorname{argmin}f\). Then \(P_{\mathrm{ss}}\) implies \(P_{\mathrm{min}}\), because a local minimizer of a \(C^2\) unconstrained objective is critical and has positive-semidefinite Hessian. The converse does not hold in general: \(P_{\mathrm{min}}\) permits nonglobal degenerate saddles whose Hessians have no negative eigenvalue. Thus a landscape satisfying \(P_{\mathrm{min}}\) but not \(P_{\mathrm{ss}}\) has only part of the favorable strict-saddle coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the smooth unconstrained setting, negative curvature at every nonglobal critical point rules out spurious local minima, but the absence of spurious local minima does not rule out degenerate nonglobal saddles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{ss}}\Rightarrow P_{\mathrm{min}}\), whereas \(P_{\mathrm{min}}\not\Rightarrow P_{\mathrm{ss}}\) in general.

notation.meaning: every nonglobal critical point has a negative Hessian eigenvalue

abla^2f(x_\star)

children.top_down_role: Saddle structures whose nonminimality appears through derivatives beyond second order.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional saddle behavior first revealed by a Taylor term above quadratic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^m\) near a critical point \(x_\star\), where \(m\geq3\). The point is an order-\(m\) higher-order saddle if \(D^j f(x_\star)=0\) for \(1\leq j<m\), and the homogeneous polynomial \(p_m(v)=D^m f(x_\star)[v,\ldots,v]/m!\) takes both positive and negative values. Then arbitrarily close to \(x_\star\) there are points with objective values above and below \(f(x_\star)\), although the gradient and Hessian at \(x_\star\) reveal no descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher-order saddle has vanishing lower Taylor terms, while its first nonzero higher-order term takes both signs and exposes nearby ascent and descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_m(u)>0>p_m(v)\) for some \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: j-th Fréchet derivative at the critical point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Taylor-based definition is mathematically sufficient to produce nearby values on both sides of the critical value and fits the leaf. However, the exact term “order-m higher-order saddle” is not standardized uniformly, and no inspectable source locator is supplied.

children.title: Flat Saddles
children.top_down_role: Saddle structures with weak or vanishing curvature along decisive directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate saddles lacking detectable negative curvature at second order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\). A critical point \(x_\star\) is a flat saddle if \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\), the Hessian \(\nabla^2f(x_\star)\) is positive semidefinite and singular, and \(x_\star\) is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum. Equivalently, every neighborhood of \(x_\star\) contains points \(x^-\) and \(x^+\) satisfying \(f(x^-)<f(x_\star)<f(x^+)\), but the quadratic model has no negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat saddle is a genuine saddle whose singular positive-semidefinite Hessian fails to display its nearby descent behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f(x_\star)=0\), \(\nabla^2f(x_\star)\succeq0\), and \(x_\star\) is not a local extremum.

children.title: Hessian-Invisibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where robust second-order tests do not expose saddle behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian-Invisibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete objectives with identical second-order data but different critical-point types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb{R}^2\), define \(f_+(x,y)=x^4+y^4\) and \(f_\pm(x,y)=x^4-y^4\). At the origin, both functions satisfy \(
abla f_+(0,0)=
abla f_\pm(0,0)=0\) and \(
abla^2f_+(0,0)=
abla^2f_\pm(0,0)=0\). Nevertheless, \((0,0)\) is a strict global minimizer of \(f_+\) and a saddle of \(f_\pm\). Thus gradient and Hessian data alone cannot classify a degenerate critical point when the first distinguishing Taylor terms have order greater than two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quartic minimum and quartic saddle share zero gradient and zero Hessian at the origin, demonstrating the Hessian's inability to classify degenerate points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_2f_+(0,0)=J_2f_\pm(0,0)\), but the two origins have different critical-point types.

notation.meaning: value, gradient, and Hessian data—the second-order jet—at x

children.title: Degeneracy Classification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of local classification under combined flatness and higher-order effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Classification Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marks where the Hessian test ceases to determine local critical-point type.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2\) near a critical point \(x_\star\). A positive-definite Hessian certifies a strict local minimum, a negative-definite Hessian certifies a strict local maximum, and an indefinite Hessian certifies a saddle. If \(\nabla^2f(x_\star)\) is singular and semidefinite, these second-order implications stop: the point may be a minimum, maximum, saddle, or belong to a stationary continuum. Classification then requires higher-order terms or additional local structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Definite or indefinite nonsingular Hessians classify critical points, while a singular semidefinite Hessian marks the boundary where second-order classification becomes inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det\nabla^2f(x_\star)=0\) with semidefiniteness implies no general second-order classification.
