children.title: Gradient-Descent Saddle Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Discrete-time avoidance for suitable gradient maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Descent Saddle Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-zero attraction to a strict saddle under a globally invertible fixed-step gradient map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\) have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, choose \(0<\alpha<1/L\), and define \(g(x)=x-\alpha
abla f(x)\). If \(x_*\) is critical and \(
abla^2 f(x_*)\) has a negative eigenvalue, then \(Dg(x_*)=I-\alpha
abla^2 f(x_*)\) has an eigenvalue larger than one. The center-stable manifold theorem and invertibility of \(g\) imply that the basin \(\{x:g^k(x)	o x_*\}\) is contained in a countable union of preimages of lower-dimensional manifolds and hence has Lebesgue measure zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-step gradient descent with a sufficiently small step almost never converges to any specified strict saddle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Leb}_n\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g^k(x)\to x_*\}=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem and content kind fit the discrete-time leaf. Under the stated global Lipschitz and step-size hypotheses, the gradient map is a global diffeomorphism and the countable-preimage null-set argument is standard, but neither result has an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measure-zero saddle avoidance by gradient descent
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)\), fix \(\alpha>0\), and define \(G_\alpha(x)=x-\alpha\nabla f(x)\). Let \(\mathcal S\) be a designated family of strict saddles.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-stepsize deterministic gradient descent under a local-diffeomorphism regime. This is asymptotic avoidance, not efficient escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Gradient descent is said to avoid \(\mathcal S\) if
\[
B_{\mathrm{GD}}(\mathcal S):=\{x_0:G_\alpha^k(x_0)\to s\text{ for some }s\in\mathcal S\}
\]
has Lebesgue measure zero. The stable-manifold form of the definition requires each saddle-convergent orbit eventually to enter a lower-dimensional local stable manifold of \(G_\alpha\), and requires the applicable inverse branches of \(G_\alpha\) to preserve null sets. At a strict saddle \(s\), a negative Hessian eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\) yields the multiplier \(1-\alpha\lambda>1\), hence an unstable discrete direction for every \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient-descent saddle avoidance means that the initial states whose iterates converge to a designated strict saddle form a measure-zero set. Negative Hessian curvature always produces a multiplier larger than one. Suitable local invertibility permits the local stable-manifold null set to be transported backward through earlier iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(s\in\mathcal S\) is a fixed point with at least one negative Hessian eigenvalue.
\(G_\alpha\) is locally invertible on the relevant preimage neighborhoods and its inverse branches preserve Lebesgue-null sets.
The saddle family is countable, or nullity of the full basin union is otherwise established.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Leb}_d(B_{\mathrm{GD}}(\mathcal S))=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every initialization law \(\nu\ll\operatorname{Leb}_d\), \(\mathbb P_{X_0\sim\nu}(G_\alpha^k(X_0)\to\mathcal S)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\nabla f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(0<\alpha<1/L\), the Jacobian \(I-\alpha\nabla^2f(x)\) is nonsingular wherever the Hessian exists.
For a single hyperbolic strict saddle, its local stable manifold has codimension at least one.
immediate_consequences_latex: Absolutely continuous initialization assigns probability zero to the saddle-convergence basin.
The property is compatible with iterates spending many steps near a weakly unstable saddle.
boundary_notes: Without suitable invertibility, backward preimages of a null local stable set require separate analysis.
A countable-union argument does not automatically cover a continuum of saddles.
Avoidance alone neither proves convergence nor identifies the eventual limit.

notation.meaning: Initial states whose gradient-descent iterates converge to the saddle family.

children.title: Random-Initialization Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Avoidance conclusions based on initialization measures and negligible stable sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Initialization Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers a null-basin geometric result into an almost-sure statement for continuous initialization laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be an iteration map and let \(S\) be a collection of undesirable fixed points. Define their combined basin by \(B(S)=\{x:T^k(x)\to s\text{ for some }s\in S\}\). If \(B(S)\) is Lebesgue measurable with \(\operatorname{Leb}_n(B(S))=0\), and the initialization law \(\mu\) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, then an initialization \(X_0\sim\mu\) satisfies \(\mathbb{P}(T^k(X_0)\to S)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any absolutely continuous initialization avoids a measurable union of saddle basins whenever that union has Lebesgue measure zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}_{X_0\sim\mu}(X_0\in B(S))=\mu(B(S))=0\).

notation.meaning: Combined convergence basin of the fixed points in the set S.
The initialization distribution is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly transfers an already-established measurable null basin into an almost-sure avoidance statement. The supplied assumptions do not themselves establish that the combined basin is null, as the scope appropriately recognizes, but a measure-theoretic source with a locator is still required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-sure avoidance under an initialization law
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,\mathcal B)\) be a measurable state space, let \(Z_t\) denote a measurable continuous- or discrete-time dynamics, let \(\mathcal S\subseteq X\) be a measurable saddle family, and let \(X_0\sim\nu\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability enters only through the initial state; the subsequent dynamics may be deterministic. The definition is distribution-relative and asymptotic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dynamics has random-initialization avoidance of \(\mathcal S\) under \(\nu\) if
\[
\mathbb P_{X_0\sim\nu}\!\left(\operatorname{dist}(Z_t(X_0),\mathcal S)\to0\right)=0.
\]
If convergence to individual points is intended, replace the event by
\[
\{X_0:\exists s\in\mathcal S\text{ such that }Z_t(X_0)\to s\}.
\]
Writing this event as the measurable basin \(B(\mathcal S)\), the defining condition is \(\nu(B(\mathcal S))=0\). When \(B(\mathcal S)\) is Lebesgue-null and \(\nu\ll\operatorname{Leb}_d\), avoidance follows for that initialization law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random-initialization avoidance means that a random initial state lands in the saddle-attraction basin with probability zero. Equivalently, the initialization measure assigns zero mass to that basin. Absolute continuity transfers any established Lebesgue-null basin result to the initialization distribution.
assumptions_latex: The saddle-attraction event \(B(\mathcal S)\) is measurable.
The absolute-continuity specialization assumes \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), \(\nu\ll\operatorname{Leb}_d\), and \(\operatorname{Leb}_d(B(\mathcal S))=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Random-initialization avoidance is exactly \(\nu(B(\mathcal S))=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\nu(B(\mathcal S))=0\iff X_0\notin B(\mathcal S)\) almost surely.
If \(\nu\) has density \(p\), then avoidance is equivalent to \(\int_{B(\mathcal S)}p(x)\,dx=0\).
special_cases_latex: Any initialization distribution with a Lebesgue density avoids a Lebesgue-null stable manifold.
A discrete initialization law supported partly on a stable manifold may assign positive probability to saddle convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: The avoidance probability is one for the complement of the saddle basin.
No independence or stochasticity after initialization is required.
boundary_notes: Absolute continuity is sufficient but not necessary; singular laws may also avoid the basin if they assign it zero mass.
A distribution with full support can still be absolutely continuous and hence avoid lower-dimensional stable manifolds.
Probability-one asymptotic avoidance provides no high-probability finite-time escape bound.

notation.meaning: The initialization law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.
Measurable basin of attraction of the saddle family.

children.title: Avoidance for Gradient-Like Method Families
children.top_down_role: Extensions to coordinate, block, proximal-like, and momentum maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Avoidance for Gradient-Like Method Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract stable-manifold criterion applicable to smooth coordinate, block, proximal-like, or momentum state maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be open and let \(T:M\to M\) be a \(C^1\) local diffeomorphism. Suppose \(z_*\) is a fixed point and \(DT(z_*)\) has at least one eigenvalue of modulus greater than one. Then every orbit that remains sufficiently near and converges to \(z_*\) begins on a lower-dimensional local center-stable manifold. If \(T\) is a global diffeomorphism, its full basin is contained in countably many diffeomorphic preimages of that manifold and is Lebesgue null. Any gradient-like method whose augmented state update satisfies these hypotheses inherits this avoidance conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth gradient-like update avoids an unstable fixed point whenever its state map is invertible and has an expanding linearized direction.
assumptions_latex: For the global conclusion, \(T\) is a global diffeomorphism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Leb}_m\{z\in M:T^k(z)\to z_*\}=0\) under the global hypothesis.

notation.meaning: Update map on the method's possibly augmented state space.
Spectral radius of the update Jacobian at the fixed point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract principle is mathematically plausible and appropriately separates the local-diffeomorphism conclusion from the global-diffeomorphism basin conclusion. It needs a specifically located center-stable theorem, and each named method family would require a separate check of its state map and invertibility hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Saddle Avoidance by a Family of Gradient-Like Maps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be measurable, let \(f\in C^2(X)\), and let \(\{T_\theta:X\to X\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\) be a family of measurable iteration maps. For \(x_0\in X\), write \(x_{k+1}=T_\theta(x_k)\). Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{x:\nabla f(x)=0\}\) denote the selected class of saddle points, and let \(\mu\) be an initialization measure on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic iteration maps with randomness entering through initialization; the definition covers coordinate, block, proximal-like, and momentum methods after their state is represented in an appropriate product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(\{T_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\) is said to avoid \(\mathcal S\) under \(\mu\) if, for every admissible \(\theta\), the basin \(W^s_\theta(\mathcal S):=\{x_0\in X:\operatorname{dist}(T_\theta^k(x_0),\mathcal S)\to0\}\) is \(\mu\)-null. Equivalently, \(\mu\bigl(W^s_\theta(\mathcal S)\bigr)=0\), so an initialization \(X_0\sim\mu\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(\operatorname{dist}(T_\theta^k(X_0),\mathcal S)\to0)=0\). For a lifted method with state \(z_k\in Z\) and primal projection \(\pi:Z\to X\), replace the basin by \(\{z_0:\operatorname{dist}(\pi(T_\theta^k(z_0)),\mathcal S)\to0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of gradient-like methods avoids a chosen saddle set when, for every admissible method parameter, the initial states whose iterates approach that set have initialization measure zero. Methods with momentum or memory are treated on their full state space and avoidance is tested through the primal projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall\theta\in\Theta,\qquad \mu\!\left(\left\{x_0:\operatorname{dist}(T_\theta^k(x_0),\mathcal S)\to0\right\}\right)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(X_0\sim\mu\), then \(\mathbb P(\operatorname{dist}(T_\theta^k(X_0),\mathcal S)\to0)=0\) for every admissible \(\theta\).
special_cases_latex: For a single map, take \(\Theta=\{\theta_0\}\).
For coordinate or block methods with a fixed update schedule, one full sweep may be used as \(T_\theta\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition concerns convergence to the saddle set and does not itself bound the time spent near that set.
boundary_notes: A parameter-uniform assertion stronger than pointwise nullity would require a common exceptional set and is not included.
Random update schedules require a path-space or Markov-kernel formulation not supplied here.

notation.meaning: Basin of initial states whose iterates approach the selected saddle set.
Projection from a lifted algorithmic state to its primal variable.

children.title: Asymptotic Avoidance versus Efficient Escape
children.top_down_role: The separation between long-run nonconvergence to saddles and quantitative departure from saddle neighborhoods.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Jin, Ge, Netrapalli, Kakade, and Jordan, How to Escape Saddle Points Efficiently
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Jin, Ge, Netrapalli, Kakade, and Jordan, How to Escape Saddle Points Efficiently

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Avoidance and Quantitative Saddle Escape
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X_k)_{k\ge0}\) be an iterative process in \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal S\) be a specified saddle set, and let \(U_r(\mathcal S)=\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal S)<r\}\). For a start time \(t\), define the exit time \(\tau_{r,t}=\inf\{j\ge0:X_{t+j}\notin U_r(\mathcal S)\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definitional separation between a long-run probability-zero convergence event and a finite-time, parameter-dependent exit guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The process has asymptotic avoidance of \(\mathcal S\) under an initialization law \(\mu\) if \(\mathbb P_\mu(\operatorname{dist}(X_k,\mathcal S)\to0)=0\). It has \((r,T,\delta)\)-efficient escape if, whenever \(X_t\in U_r(\mathcal S)\) and the stated local saddle conditions hold, \(\mathbb P(\tau_{r,t}\le T\mid\mathcal F_t)\ge1-\delta\). Thus efficient escape includes an explicit neighborhood radius, time bound, and failure probability, whereas asymptotic avoidance specifies none of them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asymptotic avoidance means that convergence to the saddle set occurs with probability zero. Efficient escape is a stronger quantitative property: conditional on entering a prescribed saddle neighborhood, the process exits within a stated number of iterations with at least a stated probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{asymptotic avoidance: }\mathbb P_\mu(\operatorname{dist}(X_k,\mathcal S)\to0)=0;\qquad \text{efficient escape: }\mathbb P(\tau_{r,t}\le T\mid\mathcal F_t)\ge1-\delta.\]
special_cases_latex: For deterministic dynamics, efficient escape reduces to \(\tau_{r,t}\le T\).
Taking \(\delta=0\) gives a sure finite-time exit guarantee.
immediate_consequences_latex: Asymptotic avoidance alone permits arbitrarily long residence in \(U_r(\mathcal S)\).
An efficient-escape statement is meaningful only after specifying the local conditions under which its quantifier applies.
boundary_notes: Efficient escape from one neighborhood does not preclude later re-entry.
Neither property alone asserts convergence to a local minimizer.

notation.meaning: First exit time after time t from the radius-r neighborhood of the saddle set.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not support this exact paired definition or its conditional exit-time formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Avoidance and Quantitative Saddle Escape

children.title: Almost-Sure Asymptotic Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Long-run avoidance without a quantitative escape-time guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Sure Asymptotic Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An asymptotic probability-one conclusion that supplies no uniform time for leaving a saddle neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(S=\{s_j:j\in\mathbb{N}\}\) be a countable family of undesirable critical fixed points, and suppose each basin \(B_j=\{x:T^k(x)\to s_j\}\) has Lebesgue measure zero. If \(X_0\) has an absolutely continuous distribution, then \(\mathbb{P}(T^k(X_0)\to s_j\text{ for some }j)=0\). This statement concerns only the limit as \(k\to\infty\); it does not imply any finite bound on the first exit time from a neighborhood of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random initialization almost surely avoids countably many null saddle basins, but the conclusion gives no quantitative escape time.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is countable and every \(B_j\) is Lebesgue null.
The law of \(X_0\) is absolutely continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(X_0\in\bigcup_{j=1}^{\infty}B_j)=0\), with no asserted bound on an exit time.

notation.meaning: Basin of attraction of the j-th undesirable fixed point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The countable-union argument is correct and the statement carefully disclaims any finite escape-time bound. The principle fits the terminal container, but no source with an inspectable locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, let \((X_k)_{k\ge0}\) be an \(\mathbb R^n\)-valued process, and let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a measurable saddle set. Randomness may arise from \(X_0\), from the iteration, or from both.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Long-run avoidance only; no quantitative residence-time or escape-time assertion is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The process almost surely asymptotically avoids \(\mathcal S\) if the event \(A_{\mathcal S}:=\{\omega:\operatorname{dist}(X_k(\omega),\mathcal S)\to0\}\) has probability zero. For an isolated saddle \(x^s\), this is \(\mathbb P(\lim_{k\to\infty}X_k=x^s)=0\). If every sample path is known to converge and all nonminimizing critical points belong to \(\mathcal S\), the definition is equivalently expressed by saying that the almost-sure limit is not in \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Almost-sure asymptotic avoidance means that the sample paths approaching the specified saddle set form a probability-zero event. For one isolated saddle, the probability of convergence to that point is zero. The definition gives no rate of departure from its neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb P\!\left(\left\{\omega:\lim_{k\to\infty}\operatorname{dist}(X_k(\omega),\mathcal S)=0\right\}\right)=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an isolated \(x^s\), \(\mathbb P(\lim_{k\to\infty}X_k=x^s)=0\).
If \(X_k\to X_\infty\) almost surely and \(\mathcal S\) is closed, the condition becomes \(\mathbb P(X_\infty\in\mathcal S)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For deterministic dynamics with random initialization \(X_0\sim\mu\), the condition is \(\mu(W^s(\mathcal S))=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No finite \(T\) or neighborhood radius \(r\) is furnished by this property.
boundary_notes: The event of visiting \(\mathcal S\) finitely many times is not excluded.
Avoidance of each saddle separately need not imply avoidance of an uncountable union without an additional argument.

notation.meaning: Event that the iterates asymptotically approach the saddle set.

review_flags: No supplied and inspected source states the exact almost-sure definition with the required distinction from escape time.

children.title: Finite-Time Saddle Escape
children.top_down_role: Quantitative departure from small-gradient negative-curvature regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Time Saddle Escape
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step quantitative decrease along a certified negative-curvature direction under a positive Lipschitz-Hessian constant; no neighborhood-exit claim is made without an additional geometric condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\) have a \(\rho\)-Lipschitz Hessian with \(\rho>0\). At \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), suppose a unit vector \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2 f(x)v\leq-\gamma\) for some \(\gamma>0\). Choose the sign of \(v\) so that \(\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}v\leq0\), and set \(s=2\gamma/\rho\). Then the third-order Taylor bound gives \(f(x+sv)-f(x)\leq-2\gamma^3/(3\rho^2)\). Thus the certified negative-curvature direction supplies an explicitly sized, objective-decreasing step; it certifies exit from a specified region only when the step geometry additionally implies such an exit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive Hessian Lipschitz constant, a certified negative-curvature direction yields an explicitly sized step and a quantified objective decrease. Leaving a particular neighborhood requires an additional geometric condition.
assumptions_latex: The sign of \(v\) is chosen so that \(\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}v\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\!\left(x+(2\gamma/\rho)v\right)\leq f(x)-2\gamma^3/(3\rho^2)\).

notation.meaning: Certified magnitude of negative curvature along the unit vector.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Time Escape from a Strict-Saddle Region
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), let \((X_k)\) be an iterative process, and fix \(\epsilon_g,\gamma,r>0\). Define the negative-curvature region \(\mathcal R_{\epsilon_g,\gamma}=\{x:\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\epsilon_g,\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\le-\gamma\}\) and the exit time \(\tau_{r,t}=\inf\{j\ge0:\|X_{t+j}-X_t\|\ge r\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative escape from small-gradient regions having curvature bounded away from zero in a negative direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The process has an \((\epsilon_g,\gamma,r,T,\delta)\) finite-time saddle-escape guarantee if, for every stopping time \(t\) with \(X_t\in\mathcal R_{\epsilon_g,\gamma}\), one has \(\mathbb P(\tau_{r,t}\le T\mid\mathcal F_t)\ge1-\delta\). A function-decrease version additionally requires \(\min_{0\le j\le T} f(X_{t+j})\le f(X_t)-\Delta_f\) for a specified \(\Delta_f>0\), with the same success probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-time saddle escape requires that whenever an iterate lies in a small-gradient region with a sufficiently negative Hessian eigenvalue, the process leaves a prescribed local ball within a stated number of iterations, except with a stated failure probability. An optional stronger version also requires a quantified objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[X_t\in\mathcal R_{\epsilon_g,\gamma}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb P(\tau_{r,t}\le T\mid\mathcal F_t)\ge1-\delta.\]
special_cases_latex: For deterministic algorithms, set \(\delta=0\).
At an exact strict saddle, \(\epsilon_g=0\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(X_t))\le-\gamma\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition supplies a quantitative guarantee absent from almost-sure asymptotic avoidance.
boundary_notes: The numerical values of \(T\), \(r\), and \(\Delta_f\) depend on the algorithm and regularity assumptions.
The definition excludes degenerate saddles when no uniform \(\gamma>0\) is available.

notation.meaning: Small-gradient region with Hessian minimum eigenvalue at most minus gamma.
First departure by radius r from the iterate at time t.

children.title: Metastability near Weak Saddles
children.top_down_role: Long transient behavior near flat or poorly conditioned unstable regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Metastability near Weak Saddles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quadratic family quantifies arbitrarily long escape transients as unstable curvature approaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_\gamma(x)=-\gamma x^2/2\) with \(\gamma>0\), fixed-step gradient descent satisfies \(x_{k+1}=(1+\alpha\gamma)x_k\). Given \(0<|x_0|<R\), the first index with \(|x_k|\geq R\) is \(\left\lceil\log(R/|x_0|)/\log(1+\alpha\gamma)\right\rceil\). Although the origin is a strict saddle for every \(\gamma>0\), this escape time diverges as \(\gamma\downarrow0\) or \(|x_0|\downarrow0\). Hence asymptotic saddle avoidance alone cannot furnish a curvature-independent or initialization-independent finite escape bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a strict quadratic saddle can retain iterates arbitrarily long when its negative curvature or the initial displacement is small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_R=\left\lceil\log(R/|x_0|)/\log(1+\alpha\gamma)\right\rceil\to\infty\) as \(\gamma\downarrow0\) or \(|x_0|\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: First iteration at which the magnitude reaches or exceeds R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metastable Residence near a Weak Saddle Region
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X_k)\) be a stochastic or randomly initialized process in \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(U\) be a measurable neighborhood of a saddle or saddle region, and define \(\tau_U=\inf\{k\ge0:X_k\notin U\}\). Let \(a(\eta)\to\infty\) be a time scale indexed by a weakness parameter \(\eta\downarrow0\), such as the magnitude of the least negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Long transient residence caused by weak instability; this is a scale-dependent property rather than convergence to the saddle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \((X_k^{(\eta)})\) is metastable in \(U_\eta\) on the scale \(a(\eta)\) if there exist constants \(0<c_1<c_2<\infty\) and \(p>0\) such that \(\liminf_{\eta\downarrow0}\mathbb P(c_1a(\eta)\le\tau_{U_\eta}\le c_2a(\eta))\ge p\). A one-sided residence formulation requires only \(\liminf_{\eta\downarrow0}\mathbb P(\tau_{U_\eta}\ge c_1a(\eta))\ge p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metastability near weak saddles means that, as the instability becomes weak, trajectories remain in a corresponding saddle neighborhood for a diverging characteristic time with probability bounded away from zero. It describes long transients, not asymptotic attraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\liminf_{\eta\downarrow0}\mathbb P\!\left(c_1a(\eta)\le\tau_{U_\eta}\le c_2a(\eta)\right)\ge p>0,\qquad a(\eta)\to\infty.\]
special_cases_latex: For a linearized unstable mode with growth factor \(1+\eta\), a natural escape scale may be proportional to \(\eta^{-1}\) times a logarithmic radius ratio, but this scaling is not part of the definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: Metastability is compatible with eventual saddle avoidance.
A uniform finite-time escape bound cannot hold on the diverging scale without additional restrictions.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert an exponential exit-time law.
Flat stationary points with no unstable mode require a different degeneracy model.

notation.meaning: First exit time from the parameter-dependent saddle neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), fix \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and set \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\in\mathbb S^n\). Let \(\gamma\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\) be curvature and residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained optimization; certificates may be exact or tolerance-qualified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(\gamma\)-negative-curvature certificate at \(x\) is a nonzero vector \(v\) satisfying \(v^THv/\|v\|^2\le-\gamma\). A \((\gamma,\varepsilon)\)-spectral certificate additionally supplies \(\theta=v^THv/\|v\|^2\) with \(\|Hv-\theta v\|\le\varepsilon\|v\|\). An exclusion certificate at threshold \(\gamma\) is verified information establishing \(H\succeq-\gamma I\), equivalently \(u^THu\ge-\gamma\|u\|^2\) for every \(u\). A certificate system is a procedure whose admissible outputs are either such a witness, such an exclusion statement, or an explicitly inconclusive result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature certificate is a direction whose Hessian Rayleigh quotient is at most minus a chosen threshold. An exclusion certificate establishes that no direction has curvature below that threshold. A certificate system may return either conclusion or declare that its computation is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{witness: }v\ne0,\ \frac{v^THv}{\|v\|^2}\le-\gamma;\qquad \text{exclusion: }H\succeq-\gamma I.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exclusion condition is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-\gamma\).
At \(\gamma=0\), a witness has \(v^THv<0\) when strict negativity is required.
special_cases_latex: At a stationary point, a strict witness excludes second-order local minimality.
A normalized witness may always be reported with \(\|v\|=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A witness immediately provides a direction of negative curvature for a quadratic local model.
boundary_notes: A small Ritz value without a validated error bound need not be an exclusion certificate.
The definition concerns unconstrained curvature; constrained problems require restriction to feasible or critical directions.

notation.meaning: Rayleigh quotient associated with the reported vector.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and suppose the complete symmetric matrix \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\) is explicitly formed and available to a matrix algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional curvature assessment using stored Hessian entries, as distinguished from Hessian-vector-product or gradient-difference access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit-Hessian certification procedure is a map applied to the entries of \(H\) that returns either a vector \(v\ne0\) with \(v^THv<0\), an inertia triple \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(n_+,n_-,n_0)\), or a validated lower spectral bound \(\underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(H)\). The procedure certifies negative curvature when \(n_->0\), when \(\underline\lambda<0\) is accompanied by a corresponding validated witness, or directly when the reported vector has a negative Rayleigh quotient. It certifies positive semidefiniteness when \(n_-=0\), equivalently \(H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit-Hessian certification uses the fully assembled Hessian matrix to compute spectral, inertia, or factorization information. Negative curvature is certified by a negative Rayleigh quotient or a positive count of negative eigenvalues; positive semidefiniteness is certified by the absence of negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[n_->0\iff\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\iff\exists v\ne0:\ v^THv<0;\qquad n_-=0\iff H\succeq0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For symmetric \(H=Q\Lambda Q^T\), the inertia counts the positive, negative, and zero diagonal entries of \(\Lambda\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\nabla f(x)=0\), a negative-curvature certificate rules out the second-order necessary condition for an unconstrained local minimum.
immediate_consequences_latex: A normalized eigenvector for \(\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\) is an exact negative-curvature direction.
boundary_notes: Floating-point computations require numerical thresholds for eigenvalues near zero.
The definition presumes the complete Hessian can be stored and accessed.

notation.meaning: Triple of counts of positive, negative, and zero Hessian eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Eigensystem Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full symmetric eigendecomposition for exact inertia and minimum-curvature certificates in dense arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a dense symmetric matrix \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), compute an orthogonal eigendecomposition \(H=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)Q^{\mathsf T}\) and order the eigenvalues increasingly. Return the inertia by counting negative, zero, and positive eigenvalues under a declared numerical tolerance. If \(\lambda_1<0\), output \(v=Qe_1\), which satisfies \(\|v\|=1\) and \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\lambda_1<0\); otherwise certify positive semidefiniteness to the chosen tolerance. Standard dense symmetric eigensolvers require \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(n^2)\) storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full symmetric eigendecomposition reports inertia and either returns a most-negative direction or certifies numerical positive semidefiniteness.
assumptions_latex: A numerical zero tolerance is fixed before classifying eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\lambda_{\min}(H)\), with dense cost \(O(n^3)\) and storage \(O(n^2)\).

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be an explicitly stored dense Hessian or symmetric model matrix. A full symmetric eigensolver returns an orthogonal matrix \(Q=[q_1,\ldots,q_n]\) and a real diagonal matrix \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full finite-dimensional spectral analysis; no sparse or matrix-free access model is intended.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dense eigensystem certification consists of computing \(H=Q\Lambda Q^T\), \(Q^TQ=I\), ordering \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\), and classifying curvature from the resulting spectrum. The minimum-curvature certificate is \((\lambda_1,q_1)\), since \(Hq_1=\lambda_1q_1\) and \(q_1^THq_1=\lambda_1\). The inertia is \((\#\{i:\lambda_i>0\},\#\{i:\lambda_i<0\},\#\{i:\lambda_i=0\})\), with numerical thresholds replacing exact signs in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense eigensystem method computes all eigenvalues and an orthonormal eigenbasis of the explicitly stored symmetric Hessian. The smallest eigenpair supplies the extremal-curvature direction, while the signs of all eigenvalues supply the inertia.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[H=Q\Lambda Q^T,\quad \lambda_{\min}(H)=\lambda_1=q_1^THq_1,\quad \operatorname{In}(H)=\bigl(\#\lambda_i>0,\#\lambda_i<0,\#\lambda_i=0\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H\succeq0\) exactly when every \(\lambda_i\ge0\).
\(H\) is indefinite exactly when the spectrum contains both positive and negative eigenvalues.
special_cases_latex: If \(\lambda_1<0\), then \(q_1\) is a unit negative-curvature certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The complete spectrum permits both extremal-curvature and inertia certification.
boundary_notes: Dense storage and full decomposition are generally unsuitable for very large \(n\).
Near-zero eigenvalues require a declared numerical sign tolerance.

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix of ordered Hessian eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Factorizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inertia and negative-curvature certificates extracted from a pivoted symmetric indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a symmetric matrix admit a nonsingular pivoted factorization \(H=PLDL^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\), where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is nonsingular lower triangular, and \(D\) is block diagonal with symmetric blocks of order one or two. Sylvester's law of inertia gives \(\operatorname{inertia}(H)=\operatorname{inertia}(D)\). If a vector \(z\) supported on a negative block satisfies \(z^{\mathsf T}Dz<0\), then \(v=PL^{-\mathsf T}z\) is directly verifiable and satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=z^{\mathsf T}Dz<0\), certifying indefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivoted LDL factorization preserves inertia, and any negative block yields a verifiable negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{inertia}(H)=\operatorname{inertia}(D)\) and \(z^{\mathsf T}Dz<0\Rightarrow (PL^{-\mathsf T}z)^{\mathsf T}H(PL^{-\mathsf T}z)<0\).

notation.meaning: Block-diagonal pivot matrix containing one-by-one and two-by-two symmetric blocks.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be an explicitly available real symmetric matrix, possibly singular or indefinite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pivoted block factorization for inertia and indefiniteness detection in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric-indefinite factorization of \(H\) is a decomposition \(PHP^T=LBL^T\), where \(P\) is a permutation matrix, \(L\) is nonsingular unit lower triangular, and \(B\) is block diagonal with symmetric \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) diagonal blocks. By congruence, \(H\) and \(B\) have the same inertia. Consequently, the signs of the eigenvalues of the small diagonal blocks determine \(\operatorname{In}(H)\); any block vector \(w\) with \(w^TBw<0\) yields a negative-curvature vector \(v=P^TL^{-T}w\) satisfying \(v^THv=w^TBw<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric-indefinite factorization expresses a permuted symmetric matrix as a congruence of a block-diagonal matrix with one-by-one and two-by-two blocks. The block signs determine the matrix inertia, and a negative block direction can be mapped back to a negative-curvature direction for the original matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[PHP^T=LBL^T,\qquad \operatorname{In}(H)=\operatorname{In}(B),\qquad w^TBw<0\Rightarrow (P^TL^{-T}w)^TH(P^TL^{-T}w)<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Indefiniteness is detected when the block spectrum of \(B\) contains both positive and negative values.
special_cases_latex: With only \(1\times1\) blocks, inertia is obtained from the signs of the diagonal pivots.
Each standard indefinite \(2\times2\) pivot block contributes one positive and one negative eigenvalue when its determinant is negative.
immediate_consequences_latex: The factorization can certify negative curvature without computing the full eigensystem of \(H\).
boundary_notes: Numerical inertia classification depends on pivoting and zero tolerances.
The factorization alone does not necessarily identify the most negative eigenvalue.

notation.meaning: Permutation used by stable symmetric pivoting.

knowledge_statements.title: Modified-Factorization Curvature Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a stabilizing correction and an explicitly controlled factorization residual to certify negative curvature of the original matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H,E,R\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and let \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(H+E=LL^{\mathsf T}+R\). Then every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\|L^{\mathsf T}v\|^2+v^{\mathsf T}Rv-v^{\mathsf T}Ev\). Consequently, any nonzero \(v\) satisfying \(v^{\mathsf T}Ev>\|L^{\mathsf T}v\|^2+|v^{\mathsf T}Rv|\) is a verifiable negative-curvature certificate for \(H\). In the exact-factorization case \(R=0\), it is sufficient that \(v^{\mathsf T}Ev>\|L^{\mathsf T}v\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified factorization certifies negative curvature of the original matrix when the correction's quadratic contribution exceeds the stabilized-factor contribution plus a margin covering the factorization residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^{\mathsf T}Ev>\|L^{\mathsf T}v\|^2+|v^{\mathsf T}Rv|\Rightarrow v^{\mathsf T}Hv<0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric stabilizing correction introduced by the modified factorization.
Computed factor of the corrected model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature Extraction from a Modified Symmetric Factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) and suppose a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization gives \(PHP^T=LBL^T\). Fix a stabilization threshold \(\delta>0\), and let \(B=Q\Lambda Q^T\) denote the inexpensive blockwise spectral decomposition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-curvature information retained while replacing an indefinite model by a sufficiently positive-definite one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Modified-factorization curvature extraction forms \(F=Q\operatorname{diag}(\tau_i)Q^T\), where \(\tau_i=0\) for \(\lambda_i\ge\delta\) and \(\tau_i=\delta-\lambda_i\) otherwise, so that \(P(H+E)P^T=L(B+F)L^T\) with \(E=P^TLFL^TP\). The indices for which \(\tau_i>0\) identify curvature below \(\delta\). If some \(\lambda_i<0\), then \(v_i=P^TL^{-T}q_i\) satisfies \(v_i^THv_i=\lambda_i<0\) and is an extracted negative-curvature certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modified indefinite factorization stabilizes the block-diagonal factor by raising eigenvalues below a positive threshold. The altered block modes reveal where stabilization was needed, and a genuinely negative block eigenmode can be transformed back into a negative-curvature direction for the original Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F=Q\operatorname{diag}(\max\{0,\delta-\lambda_i\})Q^T,\quad P(H+E)P^T=L(B+F)L^T,\quad \lambda_i<0\Rightarrow v_i^THv_i<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The support of the blockwise modification is exactly \(\{i:\lambda_i<\delta\}\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\delta=0\), only negative block eigenvalues are shifted to the semidefinite boundary.
For a \(1\times1\) negative pivot, the associated coordinate block directly supplies \(q_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Stabilization and curvature certification can reuse the same factorization.
boundary_notes: A mode modified solely because \(0\le\lambda_i<\delta\) is not a negative-curvature witness.
The extracted vector need not approximate the globally most negative eigenvector.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be available only through an oracle \(\mathcal O_H(v)=Hv\). Starting from \(q\ne0\), define the Krylov space \(\mathcal K_m(H,q)=\operatorname{span}\{q,Hq,\ldots,H^{m-1}q\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale symmetric curvature search without forming or storing the Hessian matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free curvature detector constructs a finite-dimensional search subspace \(\mathcal U_m\), typically \(\mathcal K_m(H,q)\), using calls to \(\mathcal O_H\), and returns either a vector \(v\in\mathcal U_m\setminus\{0\}\) with \(v^THv/\|v\|^2\le-\gamma\), or a lower-bound certificate valid on the searched subspace. If \(Q_m\) is an orthonormal basis, the restricted minimum curvature is \(\theta_m=\lambda_{\min}(Q_m^THQ_m)=\min_{v\in\mathcal U_m\setminus\{0\}}v^THv/\|v\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free detector accesses the Hessian only through products with vectors, builds a Krylov or other restricted subspace, and minimizes the Rayleigh quotient in that subspace. A negative restricted minimum supplies a genuine negative-curvature direction, while a nonnegative restricted result excludes negative curvature only inside the searched subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta_m=\lambda_{\min}(Q_m^THQ_m);\qquad \theta_m\le-\gamma\Rightarrow\exists v\in\mathcal U_m:\frac{v^THv}{\|v\|^2}\le-\gamma.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a Ritz vector \(y\) of \(Q_m^THQ_m\), the lifted vector \(v=Q_my\) has the same Rayleigh quotient.
special_cases_latex: Lanczos and truncated conjugate-gradient searches are matrix-free when implemented using \(Hv\) products.
immediate_consequences_latex: A negative subspace Ritz value is a valid global witness of indefiniteness.
boundary_notes: Failure to find negative curvature in \(\mathcal U_m\) does not certify \(H\succeq0\).
Finite-difference products introduce approximation error not covered by the exact-oracle definition.

notation.meaning: Minimum Rayleigh quotient on the searched subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Lanczos Extremal-Eigenvalue Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free minimum-eigenvalue approximation with Ritz directions and computable eigenpair residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric linear operator \(H\) and a unit start vector \(q_1\), perform \(k\) Lanczos recurrences to obtain orthonormal \(Q_k\), symmetric tridiagonal \(T_k\), and \(HQ_k=Q_kT_k+\beta_kq_{k+1}e_k^{\mathsf T}\). Compute a smallest eigenpair \(T_ky=\theta y\) with \(\|y\|=1\), and return \(v=Q_ky\). Then \(\|v\|=1\), \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\theta\), and \(\|Hv-\theta v\|=|\beta_ke_k^{\mathsf T}y|\). Hence \(\theta<0\) immediately supplies a negative-curvature direction, while the residual measures Ritz-pair accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos uses Hessian-vector products to approximate minimum curvature and returns both a Ritz direction and a computable residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\|q_1\|=1\), and the stated recurrence is performed without breakdown.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\theta\) and \(\|Hv-\theta v\|=|\beta_ke_k^{\mathsf T}y|\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis of the k-th Krylov subspace.
Smallest Ritz value and associated Ritz vector.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), choose a nonzero starting vector \(q_1\), and let \(Q_m=[q_1,\ldots,q_m]\) be the orthonormal basis generated by \(m\) Lanczos steps for \(\mathcal K_m(H,q_1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric matrix-free approximation of the leftmost eigenvalue and an associated curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The \(m\)-step Lanczos extremal-eigenvalue approximation is the smallest eigenpair \((\theta_m,y_m)\) of the tridiagonal projection \(T_m=Q_m^THQ_m\). The Ritz vector is \(v_m=Q_my_m\), with \(\|v_m\|=1\) and \(v_m^THv_m=\theta_m\). Therefore \(\theta_m<0\) certifies negative curvature. A residual-qualified approximation additionally reports \(r_m=Hv_m-\theta_mv_m\), whose norm measures the eigenpair residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos builds an orthonormal Krylov basis and a small symmetric tridiagonal projection. Its smallest eigenpair gives a Ritz approximation to minimum curvature; lifting the projected eigenvector produces a unit vector whose exact Hessian Rayleigh quotient equals the Ritz value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_m=Q_m^THQ_m,\quad T_my_m=\theta_my_m,\quad v_m=Q_my_m,\quad v_m^THv_m=\theta_m;\quad \theta_m<0\Rightarrow v_m^THv_m<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\theta_m=\min\{v^THv:\ v\in\mathcal K_m(H,q_1),\ \|v\|=1\}\).
special_cases_latex: If the Krylov space becomes invariant and contains a leftmost eigenvector, then \(\theta_m=\lambda_{\min}(H)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Only Hessian-vector products and the small tridiagonal eigensystem are required.
boundary_notes: A nonnegative \(\theta_m\) does not by itself exclude negative eigenvalues outside the Krylov space.
Loss of orthogonality in finite precision may require reorthogonalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Curvature Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated conjugate gradients applied to an unconstrained symmetric quadratic model, with convergence checked before curvature-triggered termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Initialize \(s_0=0\), \(r_0=g\), and \(p_0=-r_0\). At iteration \(k\), first stop successfully if the prescribed residual or model-solution tolerance is met. Otherwise compute \(w_k=Hp_k\). If \(p_k\ne0\) and \(p_k^{\mathsf T}w_k\le0\), terminate and return \(p_k\); then \(p_k^{\mathsf T}Hp_k\le0\), so \(p_k\) is a nonpositive-curvature direction. If \(p_k^{\mathsf T}w_k>0\), set \(\alpha_k=(r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k)/(p_k^{\mathsf T}w_k)\), \(s_{k+1}=s_k+\alpha_kp_k\), \(r_{k+1}=r_k+\alpha_kw_k\), and, unless the stopping tolerance is now met, set \(\beta_{k+1}=(r_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}r_{k+1})/(r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k)\) and \(p_{k+1}=-r_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated conjugate gradients check convergence before testing curvature; a nonzero generated search direction with a nonpositive Hessian quadratic form provides a nonpositive-curvature certificate.
assumptions_latex: Residual or model-solution convergence is tested before a search direction is returned as a curvature certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever curvature-triggered termination occurs, it returns \(p_k\ne0\) with \(p_k^{\mathsf T}Hp_k\le0\).

notation.meaning: Gradient residual at the current quadratic-model iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-Curvature Detection in Truncated Conjugate Gradients
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the quadratic model \(m(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\), where \(H\in\mathbb S^n\). A conjugate-gradient iteration produces trial iterates \(z_j\), residuals \(r_j=g+Hz_j\), and search directions \(d_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature detection embedded in an inexact Newton or trust-region quadratic-model solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conjugate-gradient curvature detection is the stopping rule that declares nonpositive curvature when \(d_j^THd_j\le0\) and returns the direction \(d_j\) or an algorithmically specified boundary step along \(z_j+\tau d_j\). With a strict threshold \(\gamma\ge0\), a negative-curvature declaration requires \(d_j^THd_j\le-\gamma\|d_j\|^2\). In a trust region \(\|p\|\le\Delta\), \(\tau\) is chosen so that \(\|z_j+\tau d_j\|=\Delta\) and the lower-model-value boundary intersection is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated conjugate gradients monitors the quadratic curvature along each search direction. When that curvature is nonpositive, the inner solve stops and exposes the direction; in a trust-region method, the step continues along that direction to the boundary using the better of the two intersections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_j^THd_j\le0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_j\text{ is a nonpositive-curvature direction and the CG solve is truncated}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The strict threshold test is \(d_j^THd_j/\|d_j\|^2\le-\gamma\).
special_cases_latex: At the first inner iteration with \(d_0=-g\), the returned direction is both a descent direction and a nonpositive-curvature direction when the test fires.
For positive-definite \(H\), the curvature test cannot fire in exact arithmetic.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method detects some indefinite curvature without forming \(H\).
boundary_notes: The first detected direction need not approximate the most negative eigenvector.
A zero-curvature direction is not a strict negative-curvature certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Spectral Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized block Krylov search for a low-Rayleigh-quotient direction of a symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), block size \(b\ge1\), depth \(m\ge0\), and threshold \(\varepsilon>0\), draw \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times b}\) with independent standard Gaussian entries. Form \(\mathcal K_m(H,\Omega)=\operatorname{span}\{\Omega,H\Omega,\ldots,H^m\Omega\}\), compute an orthonormal basis \(Q\), and choose a unit eigenvector \(z\) associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(Q^{\mathsf T}HQ)\). Return \(v=Qz\). If \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv\le-\varepsilon\), report detected negative curvature; otherwise report no detection at the chosen search depth. The latter outcome alone does not deterministically certify \(H\succeq-\varepsilon I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random block Krylov space is searched for its smallest Ritz value; a sufficiently negative Ritz vector certifies negative curvature.
assumptions_latex: Independent Gaussian starting vectors and products with \(H\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned unit vector satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv=\lambda_{\min}(Q^{\mathsf T}HQ)\); negativity below \(-\varepsilon\) is a valid curvature certificate.

notation.meaning: Block Krylov subspace of depth m.
Orthonormal basis of the generated subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and one-sided interpretation of nondetection fit the leaf and are mathematically coherent, but no source is supplied for the randomized block-Krylov construction or its spectral-search interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Randomized Search for Low-Curvature Spectral Subspaces
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(\xi\) be a random starting block or vector drawn from a specified distribution, and let \(\mathcal U_m(\xi)\) be the random search subspace produced using matrix-vector products with \(H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic, matrix-free detection of eigenspaces associated with small or negative eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized spectral search at threshold \(-\gamma\) and failure level \(\delta\) is a randomized procedure returning \(v\ne0\) such that, whenever \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\le-\gamma-\varepsilon\), it satisfies \(\mathbb P_\xi(v^THv/\|v\|^2\le-\gamma)\ge1-\delta\). A typical subspace realization chooses \(v\) to minimize the Rayleigh quotient over \(\mathcal U_m(\xi)\). The probability is taken over the random start and any internal randomization, with \(H\) fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized spectral search uses random starting vectors or blocks to explore low-eigenvalue subspaces. It is qualified by a curvature threshold, a spectral margin, and a failure probability: if the matrix has sufficiently negative curvature, the procedure finds a direction below the target threshold with high probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda_{\min}(H)\le-\gamma-\varepsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb P_\xi\!\left(\frac{v^THv}{\|v\|^2}\le-\gamma\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
special_cases_latex: A randomly initialized Lanczos iteration is a randomized spectral search when its output is the smallest Ritz vector.
Block random starts may target a multi-dimensional low-curvature invariant subspace.
immediate_consequences_latex: The returned vector is a deterministic negative-curvature witness once its Rayleigh quotient has been evaluated.
boundary_notes: The iteration count and probability guarantee depend on the start distribution and spectral separation.
A high-probability detection result is not a deterministic exclusion certificate when no direction is found.

notation.meaning: Spectral margin separating the true minimum eigenvalue from the target threshold.

review_flags: No inspected supplied source supports the stated high-probability randomized spectral-search contract.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Curvature Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature search in coordinates induced by a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(M\succ0\). Apply a symmetric extremal-eigenvalue or Krylov procedure to \(B=M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2}\), using operator products implemented through applications of \(H\) and solves or factorizations involving \(M\). For a nonzero returned vector \(y\), set \(d=M^{-1/2}y\). Then \(y^{\mathsf T}By=d^{\mathsf T}Hd\) and \(y^{\mathsf T}y=d^{\mathsf T}Md\). Consequently, a Ritz value \(y^{\mathsf T}By/(y^{\mathsf T}y)\le-\varepsilon\) yields \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\le-\varepsilon d^{\mathsf T}Md<0\). Stop when such a direction is found or the selected eigensolver tolerance is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SPD preconditioner transforms the generalized curvature problem while preserving the sign of every corresponding quadratic form.
assumptions_latex: Applications of \(H\) and the required operations with \(M\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative Rayleigh quotient for \(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2}\) maps to a strict negative-curvature direction for \(H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature Search under a Positive-Definite Preconditioner
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) and let \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner with \(M=R^TR\). Define the symmetrically transformed matrix \(\bar H=R^{-T}HR^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free or explicit spectral detection in a transformed metric; the preconditioner must be positive definite so inertia is preserved by congruence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A preconditioned curvature search applies a symmetric eigensolver or Krylov method to \(\bar H\), equivalently to the generalized eigenproblem \(Hv=\lambda Mv\). A transformed vector \(u\ne0\) maps to \(v=R^{-1}u\), and \(u^T\bar Hu=v^THv\), while \(u^Tu=v^TMv\). Thus a generalized Rayleigh quotient \(v^THv/(v^TMv)<0\) is a negative-curvature certificate for \(H\). The associated preconditioned Krylov space is \(\mathcal K_m(M^{-1}H,M^{-1}r_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioned curvature search examines a symmetrically transformed Hessian, or equivalently a generalized eigenproblem defined by a positive-definite metric. Negative curvature is invariant under the transformation, while the preconditioner changes the Krylov geometry and may improve spectral separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar H=R^{-T}HR^{-1},\quad v=R^{-1}u,\quad u^T\bar Hu=v^THv;\qquad \frac{v^THv}{v^TMv}<0\Rightarrow v^THv<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eigenpairs of \(\bar H\) correspond to generalized eigenpairs \(Hv=\lambda Mv\).
special_cases_latex: With \(M=I\), the definition reduces to the unpreconditioned curvature search.
immediate_consequences_latex: A positive-definite preconditioner cannot change the inertia of the Hessian under the symmetric congruence.
boundary_notes: A nonsymmetric or indefinite preconditioner does not satisfy this definition.
Preconditioning can change approximation behavior even though it preserves the existence of negative curvature.

Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x\), and suppose gradients can be evaluated while \(

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order oracle approximation to Hessian-vector products and directional curvature in smooth finite-dimensional optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The forward gradient-difference Hessian-vector approximation is \(G_h(x;v)=[
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x)]/h\). Its associated directional-curvature estimate is \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)=v^TG_h(x;v)/\|v\|^2\). A vector is declared an approximate \((\gamma,\eta)\)-negative-curvature direction when \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)\le-\gamma\) and a validated product-error bound \(\|G_h(x;v)-
abla^2f(x)v\|\le\eta\|v\|\) is available. Then the exact Rayleigh quotient is at most \(-\gamma+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order curvature approximation replaces a Hessian-vector product by a finite difference of two gradients. The resulting scalar estimates directional curvature. To make a reliable negative-curvature declaration, the estimate must be paired with an error bound; the exact curvature can then differ by at most that bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[G_h(x;v)=\frac{\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x)}{h},\qquad \widehat\kappa_h(x;v)=\frac{v^TG_h(x;v)}{\|v\|^2};\quad \widehat\kappa_h\le-\gamma,\ \|G_h-Hv\|\le\eta\|v\|\Rightarrow \frac{v^THv}{\|v\|^2}\le-\gamma+\eta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A centered variant uses \([\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x-hv)]/(2h)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\eta<\gamma\), the validated approximate direction has strictly negative exact curvature.
immediate_consequences_latex: The approximation permits matrix-free Krylov curvature searches using gradient evaluations.
boundary_notes: The forward approximation has truncation accuracy \(O(h)\) under suitable smoothness, while roundoff limits very small \(h\).
Without a validated error bound, a negative estimated quotient is not necessarily a rigorous certificate.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(x\in U\), let \(v\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\), and choose \(h\ne0\) such that \(x+hv\in U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, deterministic directional curvature estimated solely from two gradient evaluations; no Hessian is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The forward gradient-difference curvature estimate of \(f\) at \(x\) along \(v\) with increment \(h\) is \[\widehat\kappa_h(x;v):=\frac{v^T\bigl(\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x)\bigr)}{h\,\|v\|_2^2}.\] Its unnormalized quadratic-form estimate is \(\widehat q_h(x;v):=\|v\|_2^2\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)\). If \(\|v\|_2=1\), then \(\widehat q_h=\widehat\kappa_h\). A direction is declared to exhibit estimated negative curvature at threshold \(\gamma\ge0\) when \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)\le-\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable objective, compare the gradients at x and x plus h times a nonzero direction v, project their difference onto v, and divide by h and the squared norm of v. The resulting scalar estimates normalized directional curvature. It is a negative-curvature estimate at threshold gamma when it is at most minus gamma.
assumptions_latex: \(v\ne0\), \(h\ne0\), and the line segment used by the difference lies in the domain whenever an error interpretation is desired.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)=v^T(\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x))/(h\|v\|_2^2)\) is the normalized gradient-difference curvature estimate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(h>0\), \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)\le-\gamma\) is equivalent to \(v^T\bigl(\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x)\bigr)\le-h\gamma\|v\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+b^Tx+c\) with symmetric \(H\), then \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)=v^THv/\|v\|_2^2\) for every admissible \(h\ne0\).
The centered estimate replaces the numerator by \(v^T(\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x-hv))\) and the denominator by \(2h\|v\|_2^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\nabla^2f\) is continuous at \(x\), then \(\widehat\kappa_h(x;v)\to v^T\nabla^2f(x)v/\|v\|_2^2\) as \(h\to0\).
boundary_notes: The definition is directional and does not by itself approximate the smallest Hessian eigenvalue unless the direction-selection procedure supplies an appropriate vector.
Very small \(h\) may amplify gradient-evaluation and rounding errors; those errors are not included in this exact-arithmetic definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward gradient differencing supplies a matrix-free approximation to a Hessian–vector product.

abla^2f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(\{x+thv:0\le t\le1\}\), the deterministic truncation error obeys \(\lVert G_h(x;v)-

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian–vector product is approximated from two gradients, with first-order truncation error when the Hessian is Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: For the stated bound, \(\nabla^2f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz along the differencing segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_h(x;v)\) converges to \(\nabla^2f(x)v\), with norm error bounded by \(Lh\lVert v\rVert^2/2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forward and Centered Finite-Difference Hessian–Vector Products
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable on open \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with \(x\in U\), \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), and a nonzero increment \(h\) for which the sampled points belong to \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional matrix-free approximation of the vector \(\nabla^2f(x)v\) from gradients, in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-difference Hessian–vector product approximates the action of the Hessian on a requested vector by differencing gradients along that vector. The forward form uses gradients at x and x plus h v; the centered form uses gradients at x plus and minus h v.
assumptions_latex: For the standard truncation orders, \(f\) has a locally Lipschitz Hessian for the forward formula and sufficient additional smoothness for the centered formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\widehat H_h^{\mathrm F}(x)v=(
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x))/h\), with the centered analogue \(\widehat H_h^{\mathrm C}(x)v=(
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x-hv))/(2h)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The forward formula is the directional finite difference of the vector map \(\nabla f\): \(\widehat H_h^{\mathrm F}(x)v=D_{h,v}(\nabla f)(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic objective with constant Hessian \(H\), both formulas equal \(Hv\) exactly.
When \(v=0\), both expressions equal the zero vector whenever defined.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\nabla^2f\) is locally Lipschitz, then \(\|\widehat H_h^{\mathrm F}(x)v-\nabla^2f(x)v\|_2=O(|h|\|v\|_2^2)\) for fixed \(v\).
One forward product requires one additional gradient evaluation if \(\nabla f(x)\) is already available.
boundary_notes: This definition approximates a Hessian action, not the full Hessian matrix.
The centered formula has a higher evaluation cost and its improved truncation order requires stronger smoothness.
Floating-point cancellation and noisy gradients require a separate step-size model.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Eigenvector Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extremal-curvature approximation using only gradients through centered Hessian–vector surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), a point \(x\), stepsize \(h>0\), and a matrix-free symmetric eigensolver, answer every requested product in direction \(v\) by \(B_h(v)=(
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x-hv))/(2h)\). Starting from a nonzero, optionally randomized vector, run the eigensolver for a prescribed iteration budget and return a unit vector \(u\) minimizing the computed Ritz quotient. Report approximate negative curvature when \(u^{\mathsf T}B_h(u)\le-\varepsilon\). If a uniform product-error bound \(\lVert B_h(v)-
abla^2f(x)vVert\le\eta\lVert vVert\) holds on queried directions and the reported quotient is at most \(-\varepsilon-\eta\), then \(u^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(x)u\le-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free eigensolver can replace Hessian products by centered gradient differences; an error margin converts its output into certified negative curvature.
assumptions_latex: The eigensolver accesses curvature only through requested operator products.
For certification, the stated uniform product-error bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A surrogate quotient no greater than \(-\varepsilon-\eta\) yields a unit vector \(u\) with \(u^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)u\le-\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a general nonquadratic f, the map B_h(v) defined by centered gradient differences is not linear in v. It therefore cannot be supplied directly as the operator of a standard symmetric matrix-free eigensolver, and computed Ritz values or Ritz vectors are not well-defined as stated. This is a structural mathematical defect, not merely missing evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Approximation of a Minimum-Curvature Eigenvector
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:U	o\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable at \(x\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Let \(H=
abla^2f(x)\), but suppose algorithms access \(H\) only through gradient-based approximate products \(\mathcal H_h(v)=(
abla f(x+hv)-
abla f(x))/h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, matrix-free extremal-eigenvector approximation using first-order oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm R},\varepsilon_{\mathrm res}\ge0\), a unit vector \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) and scalar \(\theta\in\mathbb R\) form a first-order minimum-eigenvector approximation at \(x\) when \[\|v\|_2=1,\qquad \theta=v^T\mathcal H_h(v),\qquad \|\mathcal H_h(v)-\theta v\|_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm res},\] and \[\theta\le\inf_{\substack{u\in\mathcal K\,;\ \|u\|_2=1}}u^T\mathcal H_h(u)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm R},\] where \(\mathcal K\) is the searched Krylov or trial subspace. It is a negative-curvature approximation at threshold \(\gamma\) if additionally \(\theta\le-\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-order eigenvector approximation is a unit trial vector obtained using gradient-difference products. Its approximate Rayleigh value is nearly minimal over the searched subspace, and the corresponding approximate eigen-residual is small. A negative value below a chosen threshold makes it a negative-curvature direction.
assumptions_latex: The gradient oracle is defined at every point sampled by the product routine.
\(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonzero search subspace, typically generated by Lanczos iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((\theta,v)\) satisfies unit normalization, a residual bound, and an approximate minimum-Rayleigh condition over \(\mathcal K\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal H_h(v)=Hv\), \(\mathcal K=\mathbb R^n\), and both tolerances vanish, then \(v\) is an exact eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever \(\theta<0\), the gradient-difference operator reports negative curvature along \(v\).
boundary_notes: Subspace minimality is not global minimality unless the search space is all of \(\mathbb R^n\) or a separate spectral-error guarantee is available.
Because finite differences need not define a linear operator for fixed \(h\), the residual is an operational certificate rather than necessarily the residual of one fixed matrix.

notation.meaning: Krylov or trial subspace searched for extremal curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quality Profile of a Curvature Certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be the exact curvature matrix at a point and let a certification procedure return an outcome \(C\) using exact or approximate oracle data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional umbrella definition separating accuracy, reliability, perturbation stability, and resource cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curvature-certificate quality profile is a tuple \[Q(C)=(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{curv}},\delta,\eta_{\mathrm{stab}},N_{Hv},N_g,N_f,M,W),\] interpreted relative to a declared certificate predicate \(\mathcal P(H,C)\). It is valid when \[\mathbb P\!\left[\mathcal P(H,C)\right]\ge1-\delta,\] the reported curvature quantity differs from its target by at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{curv}}\), and every admissible perturbation \(E\) with \(\|E\|_2\le\eta_{\mathrm{stab}}\) preserves the stated sign or interval conclusion. The remaining components count Hessian–vector, gradient, and function calls, memory, and communication respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quality of a curvature certificate is specified by its curvature error, failure probability, perturbation margin, oracle counts, memory, and communication. Quality is meaningful only relative to an explicit validity predicate and resource-counting convention.
assumptions_latex: The target matrix \(H\), certificate predicate \(\mathcal P\), probability space, perturbation norm, and cost units are declared.
All quality components are nonnegative, with \(0\le\delta\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(C)\) records logically separate accuracy, probability, stability, and cost guarantees for \(C\).
special_cases_latex: An exact deterministic certificate has \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{curv}}=\delta=0\).
A purely matrix-free cost model may set matrix-assembly and factorization counts to zero while retaining \(N_{Hv}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two certificates are directly comparable only after their predicates, error conventions, probability guarantees, and cost units are aligned.
boundary_notes: A low operation count does not imply a strong certificate, and a small residual does not alone specify failure probability or finite-precision stability.
No inspected source supplied this complete multidimensional quality tuple.
review_flags: A precise authoritative source for the combined quality-profile definition is required.

children.title: Exact Inertia Certificates
children.top_down_role: Deterministic classification of curvature subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Inertia Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact symmetric-indefinite factorization certifies the dimensions of positive, negative, and null curvature subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). An exact certificate consists of a permutation matrix \(P\), a nonsingular lower-triangular matrix \(L\), and a symmetric block-diagonal matrix \(D\) with \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) blocks such that \(P^{\mathsf T}HP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\). By congruence invariance, \(\operatorname{inertia}(H)=\operatorname{inertia}(D)=(n_+,n_-,n_0)\), where the entries count positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues. The displayed factorization and the eigenvalue signs of the small blocks of \(D\) are directly checkable. In particular, \(n_->0\) certifies existence of strict negative curvature, whereas \(n_-=0\) certifies \(H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact pivoted LDL factorization reduces inertia certification to checking the signs of one- and two-dimensional diagonal blocks.
assumptions_latex: The factorization equality is interpreted in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inertia of \(D\) exactly equals that of \(H\), thereby classifying all curvature subspaces.

notation.meaning: Permutation, triangular factor, and symmetric block-diagonal factor.
Positive, negative, and zero inertia counts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact LDL^T congruence certificate and its inertia conclusions fit the terminal certificate container and are mathematically standard, but no source or specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Inertia Certificate for a Symmetric Curvature Matrix
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be a real symmetric matrix, such as \(\nabla^2f(x)\), and let its eigenvalues be counted with algebraic multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, exact-arithmetic classification of positive, negative, and null curvature subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inertia of \(H\) is \[\operatorname{In}(H):=(n_+(H),n_-(H),n_0(H)),\] where \(n_+\), \(n_-\), and \(n_0\) count respectively the positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of \(H\). An exact inertia certificate is data \(C\) from which the equality \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(p,q,r)\), with \(p+q+r=n\), is established without approximation. For a congruence factorization \(P^THP=LDL^T\) with nonsingular \(P,L\), the certificate may be the factorization together with the exact inertia of the block-diagonal \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inertia of a real symmetric curvature matrix is the triple giving its numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues. An exact inertia certificate establishes that triple exactly, commonly through a nonsingular congruence to a diagonal or block-diagonal matrix whose signs can be counted.
assumptions_latex: Any congruence factors claimed to be nonsingular are in fact nonsingular, and arithmetic is interpreted exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate determines \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(p,q,r)\) exactly and hence the dimensions of all three curvature-sign subspaces.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(n_-(H)>0\) if and only if there exists \(v\ne0\) with \(v^THv<0\).
\(H\succ0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{In}(H)=(n,0,0)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H=Q\Lambda Q^T\) is an exact orthogonal eigendecomposition, the signs of the diagonal entries of \(\Lambda\) give the inertia certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: A certificate with \(q>0\) proves the existence of a negative-curvature direction.
A certificate with \((p,q,r)=(n,0,0)\) proves strict positive curvature.
boundary_notes: A floating-point factorization is not automatically an exact certificate when eigenvalues lie near zero.
Inertia counts curvature dimensions but does not quantify the magnitudes of nonzero eigenvalues.

notation.meaning: Inertia triple of the symmetric matrix.
