children.title: Basin Connectivity
children.top_down_role: Connectivity and separation structure among attraction basins.

knowledge_statements.title: Basin Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity of attraction basins for a specified optimization dynamics or point-to-set iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a metric space, let \(T:X\rightrightarrows X\) define an iteration \(x_{k+1}\in T(x_k)\), and let \(A\subseteq X\) be an invariant target set. Its strong basin of attraction is \[\mathcal B_T(A)=\{x_0\in X:\text{every trajectory from }x_0\text{ is defined and }\operatorname{dist}(x_k,A)\to0\}.\] Basin connectivity is the property that \(\mathcal B_T(A)\) is connected, or path-connected when explicitly required. This property belongs jointly to the objective, the update mapping, and the trajectory convention; it cannot be inferred from the local Hessian at a minimizer alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basin contains initial points whose algorithmic trajectories approach a target. Its connectivity depends on both the objective and the specified dynamics, not only local curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\rightrightarrows X\) is a point-to-set iteration map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Basin connectivity means that \(\mathcal B_T(A)\) is connected under the stated trajectory quantifier.

notation.meaning: Strong basin of attraction of A under T.

children.title: Barrier-Crossing Ownership
children.top_down_role: Placement of barrier crossing and global transition analysis outside local stationarity theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Crossing Ownership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local critical-point data do not determine the energy barrier separating two minima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), and choose \(h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) satisfying \(0\le h\le1\), \(h=1\) on \([ -\varepsilon,\varepsilon]\), and \(\operatorname{supp}h\subset(-2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon)\). For \(\delta>0\), define \(f_0(x)=(x^2-1)^2\) and \(f_\delta(x)=f_0(x)+\delta h(x)\). The functions have identical germs at the strict local minima \(-1\) and \(1\). Nevertheless, for the crossing level \(\beta_f(-1,1)=\inf_{\gamma}\max_{t\in[0,1]}f(\gamma(t))\), where the infimum ranges over continuous paths with \(\gamma(0)=-1\) and \(\gamma(1)=1\), one has \(\beta_{f_0}(-1,1)=1\) and \(\beta_{f_\delta}(-1,1)=1+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two smooth objectives can agree near both minima yet have different minimum barrier heights between them; barrier crossing is therefore global, not locally owned.
assumptions_latex: \(h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\), \(0\le h\le1\), with the stated plateau and support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_0\) and \(f_\delta\) have identical local data at \(\{-1,1\}\), but \(\beta_{f_\delta}(-1,1)-\beta_{f_0}(-1,1)=\delta\).

notation.meaning: minimum maximal objective value along continuous paths from a to b
closed support of the smooth perturbation h

children.title: Local-to-Global Transfer Limits
children.top_down_role: Limits on inferring global landscape conclusions from local saddle geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Transfer Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Even complete local smooth data at a strict minimizer cannot certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(R>2\), \(M>R^2\), and \(h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) with \(0\le h\le1\), \(h(0)=1\), and \(\operatorname{supp}h\subset[-1,1]\). Define \(g(x)=x^2\) and \(f(x)=x^2-Mh(x-R)\). Because the perturbation vanishes on a neighborhood of \(0\), the functions agree there; hence every derivative of \(f\) and \(g\) at \(0\) agrees, and \(0\) is a strict local minimizer of both. However, \(0\) is the global minimizer of \(g\), whereas \(f(R)=R^2-M<0=f(0)\), so \(0\) is not a global minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical behavior in an entire neighborhood of a strict local minimizer can coexist with opposite global-optimality conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete local germs of \(f\) and \(g\) at \(0\) coincide, but \(0\in\operatorname*{argmin}g\) and \(0\notin\operatorname*{argmin}f\).

notation.meaning: a smooth perturbation supported away from the reference point zero
set of global minimizers of f on the real line
